title: Unbounded Work Extraction And Zero Work Fluctuations In A Super-Carnot Otto Information Engine
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22831v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generally, the work output of stochastic heat engines is governed by the stochastic trajectory distribution and the energy spectrum. Because the trajectory distribution depends on the thermal reservoir temperatures, the work output is not only constrained by temperature but is also susceptible to thermal fluctuations. To address these limitations, we introduce two continuous Maxwell's demons into a quantum Otto cycle, forming an Otto information engine (OIE). We demonstrate that the work output of the OIE depends solely on the energy level gap, enabling arbitrary work extraction while eliminating work fluctuations, thereby ensuring cycle-to-cycle identical work output. Furthermore, we show that the engine's efficiency can surpass the standard Carnot efficiency even after accounting for the energy cost of demon's memory erasure. Finally, we show that the OIE can deliver superior output power even when the demon's measurement time is taken into account, and the corresponding Monte Carlo simulation has been executed.
tldr: The paper designs an Otto information engine using two continuous Maxwell's demons to achieve unbounded work extraction with zero work fluctuations and super-Carnot efficiency after erasure costs.
motivation: Stochastic heat engines suffer from work output constrained by thermal reservoir temperatures and random fluctuations, limiting their reliability and performance.
method: Two continuous Maxwell's demons are incorporated into a quantum Otto cycle, forming an Otto information engine, with thermodynamic analysis and Monte Carlo simulations including demon measurement time.
result: Work output depends only on the energy level gap, enabling arbitrary work extraction with cycle-to-cycle identical work and no fluctuations; efficiency exceeds standard Carnot efficiency even after accounting for demon memory erasure, and output power remains superior when measurement time is considered.
conclusion: The Otto information engine demonstrates that information-theoretic resources can fundamentally overcome thermal constraints and fluctuations, offering a route to high-performance quantum thermal machines.

title: Overcoming The Quasi-Static Bottleneck: A Finite-Time Quantum Otto Information Engine Achieving Near-Unity Efficiency
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generally, quantum heat engines driven by Gibbs reservoirs achieve their maximum work and efficiency only in quasi-static processes, a constraint that hampers practical applications due to the resulting vanishing power output. To address this fundamental limitation, we propose a finite-time quantum Otto information engine (OIE) driven by a Maxwell's demon paired with a single Gibbs reservoir. We demonstrate that the demon's measurement and feedback control can preserve quantum coherence to extract coherent work, while harnessing quantum internal friction as a work source. Consequently, the OIE can produce work by only modulating the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian, and surpass the quasi-static limits of its conventional counterpart in the work output and the efficiency, which accounts for the energetic cost of the demon. Notably, the OIE can achieve near-perfect efficiency alongside positive work extraction in the rapid-driving regime.
tldr: The paper proposes a finite-time quantum Otto information engine driven by a Maxwell's demon that achieves near-unity efficiency and positive work in the rapid-driving regime.
motivation: Conventional quantum heat engines driven by Gibbs reservoirs attain maximum work and efficiency only in quasi-static processes, leading to vanishing power output and limiting practical use.
method: The authors introduce a finite-time quantum Otto information engine where a Maxwell's demon performs measurement and feedback control to preserve quantum coherence, extract coherent work, and harness quantum internal friction as a work source.
result: The engine can produce work solely by modulating the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian and surpasses the quasi-static limits of its conventional counterpart in both work output and efficiency, including the demon's energetic cost.
conclusion: This work overcomes the quasi-static bottleneck by demonstrating that a demon-assisted finite-time quantum Otto engine can achieve near-perfect efficiency alongside positive work extraction in the rapid-driving regime.

Unlike conventional quantum heat engines, which require two reservoirs and achieve maximum work/efficiency only in the quasi-static limit (zero power), the OIE uses measurement and feedback control by the demon to extract work from a single thermal bath. The engine cycle consists of four strokes: (1) a unitary expansion stroke where the Hamiltonian's eigenstates are modulated, (2) a measurement of the system's energy by the demon, (3) a feedback-controlled stroke that applies a unitary operation conditioned on the measurement outcome, and (4) a thermalization stroke with the Gibbs reservoir. The demon's measurement and feedback preserve quantum coherence, allowing the extraction of coherent work, and the authors show that quantum internal friction—typically a detrimental non-adiabatic effect—can be harnessed as a work source. The OIE can thus produce positive work solely by modulating the eigenstates of the Hamiltonian, without requiring a temperature difference between reservoirs.

title: The Filtering Demon: Beyond Standard Thermodynamic Bounds And Harnessing Measurement Error And Quantum Friction
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22826v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard stochastic heat engines operate blindly, enforcing work extraction protocols indiscriminately on microstates, and consequently suppressing work output, stability, efficiency. To overcome this, we propose an Otto information engine (OIE) that employs a Maxwell's demon to filter out detrimental stochastic trajectories, and demonstrate that the OIE can provide enhanced work output and stability compared to the corresponding standard Otto engine. Remarkably, even after accounting for the energetic costs of the demon, the OIE efficiency surpasses both the standard Otto limit and Carnot bound. Furthermore, by applying the fluctuation theorem of information dissipation, we derive upper and lower bounds on efficiency, confirming that our results adhere to the second law of thermodynamics. Finally, and counterintuitively, measurement errors and quantum inner friction, traditionally considered deleterious, can be harnessed as resources, which improves robustness and enables us to ignore the adiabatic strokes time.
tldr: The paper proposes an Otto information engine that uses a Maxwell's demon to filter stochastic trajectories, achieving enhanced work output and efficiency that surpasses standard Otto and Carnot bounds while respecting the second law via an information-dissipation fluctuation theorem.
motivation: Standard stochastic heat engines enforce protocols blindly, suppressing work output, stability, and efficiency. The authors aim to overcome these thermodynamic limits by incorporating measurement and feedback in the form of a Maxwell's demon.
method: They analyze an Otto information engine where a demon filters detrimental trajectories, derive upper and lower efficiency bounds using a fluctuation theorem of information dissipation, and incorporate measurement error and quantum inner friction.
result: The OIE provides enhanced work output and stability, and its efficiency surpasses both the standard Otto limit and Carnot bound even after accounting for demon costs. Counterintuitively, measurement errors and quantum friction improve robustness and allow ignoring adiabatic stroke times.
conclusion: The work extends thermodynamic bounds for information engines and shows that traditionally detrimental effects can be harnessed as resources, while remaining consistent with the second law.

title: Modular Fault-tolerant Quantum Computing On A non-CSS Code
authors: Robert Freund, Friederike Butt, C\'esar Benito, Ivan Pogorelov, Marcel Meyer, Alex Steiner, Alejandro Bermudez, Markus M\"uller, Thomas Monz
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22572v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modularization promises to break down the design and implementation complexity of large scale quantum processors into smaller manageable subtasks. In this approach, quantum channels, realized for instance through physical rerouting of qubits or quantum teleportation, connect multiple modules. Each of those modules hosts a subset of qubits, e.g. multiple logical qubits, and provides quantum operations on them. In this work, we implement for the first time all logical operations required for modular fault-tolerant universal quantum computing with a non-Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) code, the perfect [MATH] code, on a trapped-ion quantum computer. This code is the smallest quantum error-correcting (QEC) code capable of correcting any single-qubit error, making it a compact alternative to larger CSS codes. We demonstrate logical state teleportation and a full suite of fault-tolerant operations required for universal logical control, including logical state preparation, QEC with real-time feedback, logical measurements, magic-state preparation, logical entangling operations, and magic-state injection. Moreover, we characterize the logical spectator error picked up by idling logical qubits during quantum operations on distinct qubit registers and demonstrate a logical Pauli quantum process tomography that minimizes required sampling resources for logical tomography.
tldr: First experimental implementation of a full suite of fault-tolerant logical operations for modular universal quantum computing using a non-CSS perfect code on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
motivation: Modular quantum computing aims to simplify large-scale processor design, and non-CSS codes like the perfect code offer compact error correction, but full fault-tolerant logical control with such codes had not been demonstrated.
method: On a trapped-ion quantum computer, the authors implemented logical state teleportation, logical state preparation, QEC with real-time feedback, logical measurements, magic-state preparation and injection, logical entangling operations, and characterized logical spectator errors and logical Pauli process tomography.
result: They successfully demonstrated all operations required for universal fault-tolerant quantum computing with the non-CSS perfect code, including real-time QEC feedback and magic-state injection, while characterizing logical errors and minimizing sampling for logical tomography.
conclusion: This work establishes the feasibility of modular fault-tolerant quantum computing using non-CSS codes on trapped-ion platforms, providing a compact route to universal logical control.

title: Metric Self-Dual Completion And Optimal Additive Hardness For Quantum And Graph-State Distance
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the quantum code distance is NP-hard to approximate within an additive error of [MATH], for some constant [MATH], where [MATH] is the number of qubits. Our reductions are deterministic. This improves the previous square-root additive gap to [MATH] and resolves the explicitly stated linear-gap question of Kapshikar and Kundu. Our result holds for CSS codes with identical [MATH]- and [MATH]-check spaces, and with a constant rate and constant relative distance. For every fixed [MATH], there is a constant [MATH] such that hardness still holds even when every nonidentity stabilizer has weight greater than [MATH] times the quantum distance. We also improve the hardness gap of graph state distance on [MATH] vertices of Grigorescu, Jha, and Samperton from cube-root to [MATH], resolving their explicitly stated open question. Both hardness results are asymptotically optimal since both distances are at most [MATH]. Our graph state distance hardness result holds for balanced bipartite graphs with a binary adjacency matrix that is its own inverse (mod 2). Our main technique for both hardness bounds above is classical: we show how to convert any code [MATH] of length [MATH] into a self-dual code [MATH] of length [MATH] while exactly doubling the original coset metric. The conversion is deterministic and efficient. We call it the metric self-dual completion of [MATH]. It comes with a linear embedding [MATH]. The embedding doubles all Hamming distances between vectors in [MATH] and all pairwise distances between corresponding cosets. The embedding also guarantees that all codewords of [MATH] of weight at most [MATH] are exactly [MATH].
tldr: The paper proves optimal linear additive NP-hardness for approximating quantum code distance and graph-state distance using a deterministic metric self-dual completion technique.
motivation: Quantum code distance and graph-state distance are central quantities in quantum error correction and quantum information, but their approximation complexity had remained unresolved beyond weaker sublinear hardness gaps.
method: The author introduces a classical, deterministic, and efficient transformation that converts any code of length n into a self-dual code of length 2n while exactly doubling the original coset metric, then uses this metric self-dual completion to build reductions for both quantum code distance and graph-state distance.
result: Quantum code distance is shown NP-hard to approximate within an additive linear error, improving the previous square-root gap and resolving a question of Kapshikar and Kundu; graph-state distance hardness is improved from cube-root to linear, resolving an open problem of Grigorescu, Jha, and Samperton.
conclusion: Both hardness results are asymptotically optimal since the distances are at most linear, establishing strong computational limits for quantum error-correcting codes and graph states.

deep_read.detailed_summary:
This paper proves that approximating the quantum code distance within an additive error of cN (for some constant c>0) is NP-hard, where N is the number of qubits. This improves upon the previous best additive gap of Ω(√N) and resolves an open question posed by Kapshikar and Kundu. The hardness holds even for CSS codes with identical X- and Z-check spaces, constant rate, and constant relative distance. Furthermore, for any fixed λ>1, hardness persists when every nonidentity stabilizer has weight greater than λ times the quantum distance. The authors also prove that approximating the distance of graph states on N vertices is NP-hard within an additive error of Ω(N), improving a previous cube-root gap and resolving an open question of Grigorescu, Jha, and Samperton. Both results are asymptotically optimal since the distances are at most N. The graph state result holds for balanced bipartite graphs with a binary adjacency matrix that is its own inverse modulo 2.

The main technical tool is a classical reduction called the metric self-dual completion. Given any classical code C of length m, the authors construct a self-dual code A(C) of length N=Θ(m) such that the coset metric is exactly doubled. This construction is deterministic and efficient, and comes with a linear embedding τ: F_2^m → F_2^N that doubles all Hamming distances between vectors and all pairwise distances between corresponding cosets. Moreover, all codewords of A(C) of weight at most 2m are exactly τ(C). This reduction is then used to transfer known NP-hardness of approximating the classical minimum distance (or coset weight) to the quantum setting, yielding the linear additive gap.

The paper's results are significant because they establish the strongest possible inapproximability for quantum code distance under additive error, matching the trivial upper bound of N. The construction is elegant and general, and the hardness holds under stringent conditions (constant rate, constant relative distance, and large stabilizer weights). The graph state distance result similarly achieves optimal additive hardness. The work resolves two explicit open problems and provides a versatile reduction technique that may find further applications in quantum coding theory and Hamiltonian complexity.
key_contributions: Proves that approximating the quantum code distance within additive error cN is NP-hard for some constant c>0, improving the previous Ω(√N) gap and resolving the open question of Kapshikar and Kundu.

Shows hardness holds for CSS codes with identical X- and Z-check spaces, constant rate, and constant relative distance, and even when every nonidentity stabilizer has weight > λ times the quantum distance for any fixed λ>1.

Improves the hardness gap for graph state distance on N vertices from cube-root to Ω(N), resolving the open question of Grigorescu, Jha, and Samperton; holds for balanced bipartite graphs with self-inverse adjacency matrix mod 2.

Introduces the metric self-dual completion: a deterministic, efficient reduction converting any classical code C of length m into a self-dual code A(C) of length N=Θ(m) that exactly doubles the coset metric, with a linear embedding τ that doubles all Hamming distances and pairwise coset distances.
Establishes that both hardness results are asymptotically optimal since the distances are at most N.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper's core methodology is a classical reduction called the metric self-dual completion. Given an arbitrary binary linear code C of length m, the authors construct a self-dual code A(C) of length N=Θ(m) such that the coset metric (the minimum weight in a coset of the code) is exactly doubled. This is achieved via a linear embedding τ: F_2^m → F_2^N that preserves and doubles Hamming distances between vectors and between cosets. The construction is deterministic and efficient, and ensures that all codewords of A(C) of weight at most 2m are precisely the images τ(C). This reduction allows the authors to transfer known NP-hardness results for approximating the classical minimum distance (or coset weight) to the quantum setting. Specifically, they reduce from the problem of approximating the minimum distance of a classical code, which is NP-hard to approximate within a linear additive gap, to the problem of approximating the quantum code distance of a CSS code. The self-dual property ensures that the resulting quantum code has identical X- and Z-check spaces, and the doubling of the coset metric yields the linear additive gap. For graph states, a similar reduction is used, leveraging the connection between graph state distance and the minimum distance of a classical code associated with the graph's adjacency matrix. title: Gibbs Resampling Transitions And Structured Fast-measurement Protocols
authors: Daan Timmers, Benedikt Placke, Siddharth A. Parameswaran
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum Gibbs sampling algorithms generalize classical Markov chain Monte Carlo (cMCMC) methods, and prepare thermal states on quantum computers by implementing local dissipative evolution for a mixing time [MATH]. Since quantum measurements disrupt the prepared state, the rate of extracting unbiased information from the system depends on the recovery of the underlying thermal correlations. The corresponding ''Gibbs resampling'' time [MATH] is distinct both from [MATH] and from the autocorrelation time relevant to cMCMC sampling. We study this problem in effective classical models that emulate disruptive quantum measurements of local observables on extensive subsystems. When such subsystems are chosen randomly, in models with non-local order parameters we uncover a ''resampling transition'' as a function of the fraction of sites [MATH] that are measured, from [MATH] for small [MATH] to [MATH] for large [MATH], in systems of linear size [MATH]. We argue that this transition is generically absent in systems with local order parameters, and relate this dichotomy to one between the coarsening of initial states that break 1- and 0-form symmetries under Glauber dynamics. Finally, we devise a structured fast-measurement protocol that evades slow resampling even with non-local order parameters, while leaving only a vanishing fraction of all sites unmeasured.

title: Asymmetric Two-Way Gaussian Quantum Steering In Coupled Lossy Waveguides
authors: Hafsa Zia, Haleema Sadia Qureshi, Shakir Ullah, Mohamed Amazioug, Fazal Ghafoor
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22815v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum steering is an important type of quantum correlation with potential applications in one-sided device-independent (1SDI) quantum information protocols. In this contribution, we explore the time-dependent dynamics of Gaussian quantum steering in coupled lossy optical waveguides using the covariance matrix formalism. Optical dissipation is explicitly incorporated to account for realistic propagation losses in coupled waveguides. We systematically investigate the influence of the optical loss rate, purity, nonclassicality, and squeezing of the input Gaussian states on the generation and evolution of steering. The results demonstrate that increasing nonclassicality and squeezing enhances Gaussian steering, while optical loss and reduced purity progressively suppress it. However, a considerable amount of steering can persist over finite propagation intervals in the presence of optical loss. We further examine that steering is symmetric for input states with identical nonclassicality, while unequal nonclassicalities lead to directional steering asymmetry, offering a way to control the steering direction through input-state engineering. These results demonstrate that coupled optical waveguides can support controllable Gaussian quantum steering under practical loss conditions and offer a promising integrated-photonic platform for asymmetric quantum-information protocols, including 1SDI quantum key distribution (QKD) and quantum communication.

motivation: Quantum steering enables one-sided device-independent quantum information protocols, but realistic propagation losses in integrated photonic platforms can degrade it, motivating a detailed characterization.
method: Using the covariance matrix formalism, the authors model two-mode Gaussian states in coupled waveguides with optical dissipation and analyze steering via Gaussian steering measures.
result: Increasing nonclassicality and squeezing enhances steering, while optical loss and reduced purity suppress it; asymmetric input nonclassicalities produce directional steering asymmetry, and some steering persists over finite propagation intervals despite loss.
conclusion: Coupled lossy waveguides can support controllable asymmetric Gaussian steering, suggesting a promising integrated-photonic platform for 1SDI QKD and quantum communication.

title: Extracting Electromagnetic Bare Mode Couplings In Large Superconducting Quantum Processors
authors: Reza Molavi, Ebrahim Forati, Yaxing Zhang, Andrey R. Klots, Juan Atalaya, Brandon W. Langley, Dogan A. Timucin, Moein Nazari, Ghazi Khan, Zlatko K. Minev, Alexander N. Korotkov, Michel H. Devoret
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: High-fidelity control of superconducting quantum processors requires accurate characterization of electromagnetic coupling strengths among the device's constituent elements. Accurately extracting these couplings across large-scale architectures, presently featuring hundreds of qubits, poses a challenging multi-scale modeling problem. This requires resolving scales from the nanometer-scale geometry of Josephson junctions and their leads to the centimeter-scale size of the enclosing metallic packages. We present four numerical coupling extraction methods based on the avoided level crossing, the energy participation ratio, the induced electromotive force, and the impedance matrix. These methods are tailored to work with commercially available 3D electromagnetic solvers. We benchmark these techniques on a [MATH] array of transmon qubits, extracting their couplings to standing package modes. Our results show that these methods yield consistent coupling strengths with a maximum relative difference of less than 5%.

method: Four coupling extraction methods based on avoided level crossing, energy participation ratio, induced electromotive force, and impedance matrix are tailored for commercial 3D electromagnetic solvers and benchmarked on a transmon qubit array.

conclusion: The proposed numerical techniques provide a reliable approach for extracting couplings in large-scale superconducting quantum processors, facilitating accurate device characterization and control.

title: High-Q Magneto-Optical Microdisk Resonators Based On Monocrystalline Bismuth-substituted Yttrium Iron Garnets
authors: Takeru Yambe, Kota Taniguchi, Tatsuya Kitai, Daisuke Sato, Syuan Gao, Hajime Kumazaki, Shun Fujii, Takasumi Tanabe, Satoshi Iwamoto, Yasutomo Ota
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microresonators based on diverse material platforms have driven the progress of integrated photonics by enhancing light-matter interactions in compact volumes. Extending this strategy to magneto-optical (MO) media is highly attractive for nonreciprocal photonics, magnonics, and quantum transduction, yet compact high-Q resonators based on single-crystalline yttrium iron garnet (YIG) have remained elusive because of the difficulty of its nanofabrication. Here we demonstrate high-Q, small-mode-volume MO microdisk resonators based on monocrystalline Bi-substituted YIG (Bi:YIG). Low-loss Bi:YIG thin films prepared by bonding and thinning, combined with optimized Ar-plasma etching, enable submicron-thick, air-suspended microdisks that support telecom-band whispering-gallery modes with [MATH], a mode volume [MATH] cubic wavelengths, and [MATH], representing an orders-of-magnitude improvement for integrated high-Q YIG MO cavities. The device exhibits clear magnetic-field-dependent spectral responses, including reciprocal resonance shifts and nonreciprocal frequency splitting of counter-propagating modes. A perturbative analytical model quantitatively reproduces these responses and indicates an effective MO coefficient about twice the bulk value, suggesting a possible miniaturization-induced enhancement. These results establish monocrystalline YIG microdisks as a compact high-Q MO platform for integrated isolators, optomechanics, microcombs, and photon-magnon quantum interfaces.

title: Collective Chirped Stirap In A Pair Of Three-Level Atoms: Dressed-Manifold Dynamics And Compensation Of The Rydberg-Rydberg Interaction-Induced Detuning

abstract: ArXiv:2609.22673v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate collective chirped stimulated Raman adiabatic passage (STIRAP) in a pair of identical three-level atoms using a symmetric six-state model. Numerical simulations reveal a pronounced oscillatory dependence of the population transfer to the doubly excited Rydberg state on the peak Rabi frequency, indicating dynamics beyond the conventional single-dark-state description of STIRAP. To identify the underlying mechanism, we develop a dressed-manifold description based on gauge-invariant projections onto nearly degenerate instantaneous dressed manifolds. The analysis demonstrates that the wavefunction remains predominantly confined to a two-dimensional dark manifold while becoming transiently coupled to a neighboring bright manifold during the pulse-overlap interval. We further show that in the dressed-manifold representation, the Rydberg-Rydberg interaction modifies the collective resonance structure while preserving the dark-bright manifold dynamics responsible for the oscillatory transfer; an appropriately chosen frequency chirp compensates the interaction-induced detuning and restores efficient population transfer. title: Localizable Bipartite Rank-One Ideal Measurements Have A Block-Replicated Nice-Bell Structure
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22181v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a complete structural characterization of finite-dimensional bipartite rank-one ideal projective measurements that are localizable without communication in the sense of Akibue and Miyazaki. Up to local-unitary equivalence, every such measurement basis is obtained by replicating a single nice Bell basis across equal-dimensional local subspace blocks. The necessity proof combines the causal block structure of complete measurements established by Beckman, Gottesman, Nielsen, and Preskill with their eigenstate-composition theorem for localizable superoperators. A reference block is first forced to be a nice Bell basis; the same theorem then propagates that basis consistently along every row, column, and interior block. The converse follows from the explicit localization protocol of Akibue and Miyazaki. This establishes their Conjecture 1 and gives a protocol-independent classification of bipartite rank-one ideal measurements in this setting.

method: Combining the causal block structure of complete measurements with the eigenstate-composition theorem for localizable superoperators, the authors force a reference block to be a nice Bell basis and propagate it along rows, columns, and interior blocks.
result: They establish a complete classification: every such measurement basis is obtained by replicating a single nice Bell basis across equal-dimensional local subspace blocks, confirming Conjecture 1.
conclusion: This provides a protocol-independent characterization of bipartite rank-one ideal localizable measurements and settles the conjecture.

For [MATH] both the mean lifetime and its variance are finite, for [MATH] the mean lifetime remains finite but lifetime fluctuations become infinitely broad, and for [MATH] the mean lifetime itself diverges. title: Neural Network-based Multipartite Entanglement Classification With Prior Guidance From Quantum Uncertainty Relations
authors: Qiyi Li, Xiao Zheng, Guofeng Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum entanglement is a crucial resource in quantum information processing, yet its efficient, scalable and robust classification in multipartite systems remains theoretically challenging. Although supervised machinelearning has been applied to this task, most existing methods still suffer from high measurement costs, computational consumption, and weak noise robustness. In this work, by incorporating multipartite uncertainty relations as prior guidance, we propose a neural network approach to classify distinct Stochastic Local Operations and Classical Communication (SLOCC) multipartite entanglement classes based on states sampled from their local unitary (LU) orbits. Compared with traditional techniques, our method reduces experimental measurement-resource requirements and computational overhead, showing high adaptability to large-scale systems. The classification accuracy of our method reaches 99.5% in 20-qubit systems. The numerical validation is performed on states generated by random LU transformations, which preserve the SLOCC class. Within this setting, the proposed method offers strong effectiveness, scalability, and robustness for multipartite entanglement classification.

title: Gaussian Quantum Reservoir Computing With A Hybrid Cavity Magnomechanical System
authors: Hajar Assil, Khadija El Anouz, Abderrahim El Allati, Gian Luca Giorgi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a quantum reservoir computing framework based on a hybrid cavity magnomechanical system in the linearized Gaussian regime. The reservoir combines microwave-cavity, magnon, and mechanical degrees of freedom, and is extended by an auxiliary cavity acting as an input port, with time-dependent signals encoded in its detuning. The covariance matrix of the quadrature fluctuations provides the features for a trained linear readout. Using linear-memory, nonlinearmemory, and parity-check benchmarks, we find strong temporal memory together with more limited nonlinear processing, whose balance is controlled by the reservoir evolution time, and we show that intermode correlations substantially enhance the information accessible to the readout. The same architecture reconstructs a time-dependent signal encoded in the auxiliary-cavity detuning, with an accuracy governed by the interplay between the internal couplings and the encoding strength, and robust against Gaussian detuning noise. Accounting for finite measurement statistics reveals a trade-off between encoding strength and the precision of the covariance estimation, so that the optimal encoding depends on the available measurement budget. These results establish hybrid cavity magnomechanical systems as a promising platform for continuous-variable quantum reservoir computing with potential applications in signal probing.

motivation: To exploit hybrid magnon-photon-phonon platforms for temporal information processing and signal reconstruction, addressing the need for physical reservoirs in quantum machine learning.
method: The reservoir combines microwave-cavity, magnon, and mechanical modes, with an auxiliary cavity for input encoding; the covariance matrix of quadrature fluctuations provides features for a trained linear readout, benchmarked on memory and parity-check tasks.

title: Every Architecture Of Six Two-qubit Gates Is Locally Universal On Three Qubits
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22176v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present the analytical determination of the exact accessible dimension for every fixed architecture of arbitrary two-qubit gates on three qubits. A support word represents which pair of qubits each two-qubit gate acts on, and its reduced length is obtained by merging consecutive gates on the same pair. If the reduced length is [MATH], then the set of implementable three-qubit unitaries has accessible dimension [MATH]. Consequently, six arbitrary two-qubit gates are : every fixed architecture reaches a nonempty open subset of [MATH] when its reduced length is at least six. The result is stronger than existence of one favorable architecture. Every reduced six-slot support word is locally universal, including the alternating nearest-neighbor line [MATH]. The upper bound follows from a standard parameter-counting argument. The matching lower bounds are proved by Jacobian certificates in the Pauli basis. Up to qubit relabeling and reversal, there are [MATH] reduced architectures of lengths two through six. For each one, a product of rational Pauli rotations yields a nonzero maximal minor modulo the prime [MATH]. Thus, any obstruction to global universality with six two-qubit gates must go beyond parameter counting, connectivity, and differential rank.
tldr: The paper analytically determines the exact accessible dimension for every fixed architecture of two-qubit gates acting on three qubits, proving that all reduced six-slot architectures are locally universal.
motivation: Universality of gate architectures is usually established by exhibiting one favorable arrangement or by loose parameter counting, leaving open whether obstructions beyond counting exist for short gate sequences.
method: Support words encode which qubit pair each two-qubit gate acts on; reduced length follows from merging consecutive same-pair gates. Upper bounds come from parameter counting, while matching lower bounds are proved via Jacobian certificates in the Pauli basis using products of rational Pauli rotations whose maximal minors are nonzero modulo a prime.
result: The accessible dimension equals the reduced length, so six arbitrary two-qubit gates always reach a nonempty open subset of SU(8); every reduced length-six architecture, including the alternating nearest-neighbor line, is locally universal.
conclusion: Any obstruction to global universality with six two-qubit gates must go beyond parameter counting, connectivity, and differential rank, and a full classification of the 17 reduced architectures of lengths two through six is provided.

deep_read.detailed_summary:
This paper provides the first exact analytical determination of the accessible dimension for every fixed architecture of arbitrary two-qubit gates acting on three qubits. The architecture is encoded by a support word, which specifies the pair of qubits each gate acts on; its reduced length r is obtained by merging consecutive gates on the same pair. The main result is that the set of implementable three-qubit unitaries has accessible dimension d(w) = min{63, 9r + 9}. This implies that six arbitrary two-qubit gates are necessary and sufficient for local universality: any fixed architecture with reduced length at least six reaches a nonempty open subset of SU(8). The result is stronger than merely exhibiting one favorable architecture—every reduced six-slot support word is locally universal, including the alternating nearest-neighbor line AB, BC, AB, BC, AB, BC.

The upper bound d(w) ≤ min{63, 9r + 9} follows from a standard parameter-counting argument: each two-qubit gate contributes at most 9 parameters (since SU(4) has dimension 15, but the accessible dimension counts independent directions in the tangent space of SU(8) generated by the gates). The matching lower bounds are proved by constructing Jacobian certificates in the Pauli basis. Up to qubit relabeling and reversal, there are 22 reduced architectures of lengths two through six. For each, the authors exhibit a product of rational Pauli rotations that yields a nonzero maximal minor modulo the prime 1,000,003, thereby certifying that the Jacobian has full rank and the accessible dimension is exactly 9r + 9 (capped at 63). This shows that any obstruction to global universality with six two-qubit gates must go beyond parameter counting, connectivity, and differential rank.

The paper is 80 pages long, indicating extensive technical detail, including explicit certificates for all 22 architectures. The results settle a fundamental question in quantum control and circuit synthesis: how many arbitrary two-qubit gates are needed to achieve local universality on three qubits, and what is the exact dimension of the reachable set for any given architecture. The work bridges algebraic geometry, Lie theory, and quantum information, providing a complete classification for the three-qubit case.
key_contributions: First exact analytical formula for the accessible dimension of any fixed two-qubit gate architecture on three qubits: d(w) = min{63, 9r + 9}, where r is the reduced length of the support word.

Proof that six arbitrary two-qubit gates are necessary and sufficient for local universality on three qubits, and that every reduced six-slot support word achieves local universality, including the alternating nearest-neighbor line.

Construction of explicit Jacobian certificates in the Pauli basis for all 22 reduced architectures of lengths two through six, using rational Pauli rotations and nonzero maximal minors modulo the prime 1,000,003.

Demonstration that any obstruction to global universality with six two-qubit gates must transcend parameter counting, connectivity, and differential rank, thereby sharpening the boundary between local and global universality.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The methodology combines combinatorial encoding of gate architectures with algebraic and differential-geometric techniques. The support word representation reduces the problem to a finite set of architectures, and the reduced length r captures the minimal number of alternating gate pairs. The upper bound on accessible dimension is obtained by a standard parameter-counting argument: each two-qubit gate contributes at most 9 independent parameters to the tangent space of SU(8), and the total accessible dimension cannot exceed 63 (the dimension of SU(8)). The lower bound is established by constructing explicit Jacobian certificates. For each of the 22 reduced architectures, the authors choose a product of rational Pauli rotations (i.e., gates of the form exp(iθP) with P a Pauli operator) and compute the Jacobian matrix of the map from gate parameters to the resulting unitary. They then exhibit a maximal minor that is nonzero modulo the prime 1,000,003, which certifies that the Jacobian has full rank over the rationals. This modular arithmetic approach avoids symbolic computation blow-up and provides rigorous, verifiable certificates. The use of Pauli rotations is natural because they form a basis for the Lie algebra and allow explicit rational parameterizations.
deep_read.results_analysis: The central result is the exact formula d(w) = min{63, 9r + 9}. For r = 6, this gives d(w) = min{63, 63} = 63, meaning the accessible dimension equals the full dimension of SU(8), so the architecture is locally universal. For r < 6, the accessible dimension is strictly less than 63, so local universality is impossible. The threshold r = 6 is therefore sharp. The paper enumerates 22 reduced architectures of lengths two through six (up to relabeling and reversal) and provides certificates for each. The alternating nearest-neighbor line AB, BC, AB, BC, AB, BC is explicitly shown to be locally universal. The modular prime 1,000,003 is used to ensure that the maximal minors are nonzero; this is a computational device to certify rank over the rationals. The results imply that six two-qubit gates are necessary and sufficient for local universality, and that no architecture with fewer than six reduced gates can achieve it. The paper also notes that global universality (i.e., reaching all of SU(8)) may still fail for some architectures despite local universality, and that any such obstruction must involve phenomena beyond parameter counting, connectivity, and differential rank.

limitations: The study is restricted to three qubits; generalization to more qubits is not addressed and may involve additional complexity.

The certificates rely on a specific prime (1,000,003) and rational Pauli rotations; while this proves rank over the rationals, it does not directly address whether the same architectures achieve global universality or what the exact global reachable set is.

title: Concatenated Composite Pulses Beyond Local Residual-Error Preservation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Residual-error preservation (REP) provides a sufficient rule for constructing concatenated composite pulses that compensate multiple systematic errors. We show that local REP is not necessary: deviations from REP can cancel across the full sequence. Using first-order error generators, we derive a necessary and sufficient condition for concatenation to retain the robustness of an outer sequence. A simple sufficient condition is that all inner pulses rescale the corresponding elementary error generators by a common real factor, not necessarily unity. We illustrate this principle using pulse-length and off-resonance errors, two systematic error models commonly considered in magnetic resonance. Short CORPSE and SCROFULOUS each compensate one error without preserving the other locally. Combining these inner pulses with suitable equal-rotation-angle outer sequences yields simultaneous first-order compensation of both errors, extending concatenated composite-pulse design beyond local REP.
tldr: The paper shows that local residual-error preservation (REP) is not necessary for concatenated composite pulses to be robust, deriving a general necessary and sufficient condition based on first-order error generators.
motivation: Concatenated composite pulses are a standard tool for suppressing systematic control errors (e.g. pulse-length and off-resonance errors) in magnetic resonance and qubit control, but the existing local REP design rule is overly restrictive and misses valid robust sequences.
method: Using first-order error generators, the authors derive a necessary and sufficient condition under which concatenation preserves the robustness of an outer sequence, and identify a simple sufficient condition requiring inner pulses to rescale elementary error generators by a common real factor.
result: Short CORPSE and SCROFULOUS pulses, which each locally compensate only one error, can be combined with equal-rotation-angle outer sequences to achieve simultaneous first-order compensation of both pulse-length and off-resonance errors.
conclusion: The work generalizes concatenated composite-pulse design beyond local REP, broadening the space of sequences that yield multi-error robust quantum control.

REP requires that each inner pulse in a concatenated sequence preserves the residual error of the outer sequence to first order. The authors show that REP is not necessary: deviations from REP can cancel across the full sequence. Using first-order error generators, they derive a necessary and sufficient condition for concatenation to retain the robustness of an outer sequence. A key simplification is a sufficient condition: all inner pulses must rescale the corresponding elementary error generators by a common real factor (not necessarily unity). This allows inner pulses that individually do not preserve the error to still yield robust concatenation when combined appropriately.

The work illustrates this principle with two systematic error models common in magnetic resonance: pulse-length errors and off-resonance errors. The authors analyze two well-known composite pulses: Short CORPSE (compensates off-resonance but not pulse-length) and SCROFULOUS (compensates pulse-length but not off-resonance). Neither preserves the other error locally. By combining these inner pulses with suitable equal-rotation-angle outer sequences, the authors achieve simultaneous first-order compensation of both errors. This extends concatenated composite-pulse design beyond the local REP framework.

The paper provides a theoretical foundation for designing CCPs that compensate multiple errors without requiring each inner pulse to preserve the outer sequence's error robustness. The results are derived analytically and supported by a simple example, demonstrating the practical utility of the relaxed condition. The work has implications for quantum control, magnetic resonance, and any field where composite pulses are used to combat systematic errors.

title: Exact Ballistic Energy Transport And Emergent Xxz Dynamics In An Integrable Three-state Chain
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the coupling dependence of ballistic energy transport and the emergent spin dynamics in an integrable Hermitian three-state chain that connects a clock interaction to a highly degenerate flag limit. By constructing a regular [MATH]-matrix to establish a globally conserved energy current, we analytically evaluate its full variance to obtain the exact, strictly positive leading high-temperature coefficient of the thermal Drude weight and the ballistic growth rate of the energy-correlation second moment. In the strong-coupling limit, the degeneracy is lifted by virtual transitions of a delocalized third-color spectator state, which generates an effective spin-[MATH] XXZ Hamiltonian with anisotropy [MATH] and fundamentally selects the all-active two-color sector as the true ground state. For periodic boundaries, this virtual spectator motion introduces a positive length-changing XXZ supercharge squared that, for [MATH], strictly annihilates all states within a finite, length-independent energy interval above the ground state. Consequently, we rigorously prove that the full periodic effective theory perfectly replicates the exact low-energy XXZ spectrum, including all state multiplicities, as well as its macroscopic bulk free-energy density.

motivation: To understand the coupling dependence of ballistic energy transport and the emergent spin dynamics in an integrable Hermitian chain that interpolates between a clock interaction and a highly degenerate flag limit.
method: Constructs a regular M-matrix to establish a globally conserved energy current, analytically evaluates its variance to obtain the exact thermal Drude weight and ballistic growth rate, and derives an effective XXZ Hamiltonian in the strong-coupling limit.
result: Obtains the exact positive leading high-temperature coefficient of the thermal Drude weight and the ballistic growth rate; shows that virtual transitions of a delocalized third-color spectator state generate an effective spin-1/2 XXZ Hamiltonian with anisotropy and select the all-active two-color sector as the true ground state; proves that the periodic effective theory replicates the exact low-energy XXZ spectrum and bulk free-energy density.
conclusion: The integrable three-state chain exhibits exact ballistic energy transport, and its strong-coupling dynamics are captured by an emergent XXZ model with a rigorously established low-energy correspondence.

title: Characterizing Local Unitary Equivalence Of Multipartite States By Local Unitary Bargmann Invariants
authors: Yi Shen, Lin Chen, Shao-Ming Fei
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22902v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local unitary (LU) equivalent states are crucial for understanding the structure of quantum entanglement. We investigate the LU equivalence based on the LU Bargmann invariants (LUBIs). We consider for which states the LUBIs are sufficient to ensure the LU equivalence. We focus on a class of multipartite states with complete local commutativity, called CLC states. We first show that for multipartite CLC states, all the LUBIs are sufficient to ensure the local permutation equivalence, if their single-party marginals are diagonal and non-degenerate. By virtue of the fact that the CLC property remains unchanged under local operations, we verify that the LUBIs are also sufficient to ensure the LU equivalence of multipartite CLC states whose single-party marginals are non-degenerate. Furthermore, when the single-party marginals are degenerate, we propose concrete examples of two-qudit and three-qubit systems, showing that there are states which share all the LUBIs but are not LU equivalent.
tldr: The paper studies when local unitary Bargmann invariants are sufficient to characterize local unitary equivalence of multipartite states, focusing on CLC states.
motivation: Local unitary equivalence is central to understanding entanglement structure, and it is important to determine whether known LU invariants form a complete set for this classification.
method: The authors analyze LU Bargmann invariants for multipartite CLC states with diagonal non-degenerate single-party marginals and show sufficiency for local permutation equivalence, then extend the argument to LU equivalence under non-degeneracy.
result: For CLC states with non-degenerate marginals, the LUBIs are sufficient for LU equivalence, but for degenerate marginals they construct two-qudit and three-qubit counterexamples sharing all LUBIs yet not LU equivalent.
conclusion: The work clarifies the power and limitations of LUBIs for multipartite entanglement classification, showing sufficiency in a restricted non-degenerate setting and failure in the degenerate case.

title: Efficient Creation Of Shallow Nv$^-$ Ensembles By High-angle Ion Implantation
authors: Kento Sasaki, Hideyuki Watanabe, Tokuyuki Teraji, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Kensuke Kobayashi
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV[MATH]) centers located a few nanometers below the diamond surface are key quantum defects for nanoscale sensing of external spins. By implanting [MATH]N ions at angles exceeding 60[MATH], we achieve high NV[MATH] yields approaching 10% with effective NV[MATH] depths below 10 nm. These yields are significantly higher than those typically reported for shallow NV[MATH] creation. The enhanced NV[MATH] yield is consistent with an increased vacancy-to-nitrogen ratio in the near-surface region, which is expected to promote NV formation during annealing. The created NV[MATH] ensembles show coherence properties comparable to those of single shallow NV[MATH] centers at similar depths, and allow detection of nuclear spins in van der Waals materials attached to the diamond surface. title: Spin-Boson Mappings In The Formalism Of $f$-Deformations
authors: Vladimir A. Orlov, Liubov A. Markovich, Alexey V. Mikheenkov, Vladimir I. Man'ko
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22502v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a unified algebraic approach to spin-boson transformations based on the formalism of [MATH]-deformed oscillators. In the single-mode case, we show that the Holstein-Primakoff and Dyson-Maleev transformations, together with the interpolating [MATH]-family, arise as different factorizations of the same algebraically determined object. The standard spin-boson mappings can thus be interpreted as realizations of a common structure, which makes it possible to clearly separate the exact algebraic content on the physical subspace from effects associated with non-Hermiticity, the choice of metric, and extensions beyond the physical subspace. In the two-mode case, the same approach yields both deformed versions of the Jordan-Schwinger transformation and new exact two-mode realizations. Our results provide a unified description of known spin-boson transformations and naturally lead to new bosonic representations.
