title: Secure Quantum Metasurfaces For Direct Quantum Key Distribution Measurements
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) can deliver information-theoretic security, but its receivers are still typically assembled from cascaded bulk optics. Metasurfaces offer a radical reduction in this complexity. Here, we make the metasurface function as the QKD measurement device itself. We design wavelength-specific dielectric apertures at 780, 1550, 2000, and 10 600 nm that interweave the linear H/V and circular R/L phase libraries at a 0.44--0.49{\lambda} cell pitch, i.e., below half the operating wavelength, and map the complete passive-BB84 measurement directly onto four detector channels. This subwavelength basis co-location prevents an ordinary propagating-wave aperture mask from isolating one basis without simultaneously attenuating or perturbing the other. Simulated full-wave focal-plane intensities are converted directly into conditional Born probabilities using fitted, calibration-fixed detector regions. The selected designs achieve probability fidelities of 97.96--99.08%, four-port collected efficiencies of 17.43--40.94%, and mean intrinsic quantum bit error rates of 1.42--3.96%. At 1550 nm, the selected design gives an asymptotic device-level yield of 0.151 secret bits per incident photon under an ideal single-photon model. Six-state detector tomography gives positive both-basis security bounds for all six reconstructed receiver models, including their polarization-dependent loss, basis imbalance and crosstalk. These results establish protocol-matched meta-optics as a route to compact, passive QKD receivers.
tldr: The paper designs subwavelength dielectric metasurfaces that implement a complete passive BB84 polarization measurement directly on four detector channels, achieving high probability fidelities and low intrinsic QBER as a compact QKD receiver.
motivation: QKD receivers are typically bulky cascaded-optics assemblies, and metasurfaces could radically reduce their complexity by performing the measurement function itself rather than merely acting as a focusing element.
method: Wavelength-specific dielectric apertures at 780, 1550, 2000 and 10600 nm interweave linear H/V and circular R/L phase libraries at a 0.44–0.49 lambda cell pitch, with full-wave focal-plane intensities converted into conditional Born probabilities and validated via six-state detector tomography.
result: Simulated designs reach probability fidelities of 97.96–99.08%, four-port collected efficiencies of 17.43–40.94%, mean intrinsic QBERs of 1.42–3.96%, and an asymptotic 1550 nm yield of 0.151 secret bits per incident photon.
conclusion: Protocol-matched meta-optics is proposed as a viable route toward compact, passive, basis-co-located QKD receivers, though the work remains a simulated device-level design without experimental demonstration or new protocol theory.

title: Universal Response Functions In Driven Dissipative Tunneling Dynamics
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Universality in nonlinear nonequilibrium systems is typically expressed through scaling laws that render macroscopic behavior insensitive to microscopic details. Whether this universality survives when periodic forcing and nonlocal dissipative memory act simultaneously remains an open question in driven open dynamics. Here, we demonstrate that barrier-crossing processes in periodically driven dissipative systems are governed not merely by modified exponential scaling, but by an explicit two-parameter universal response function. Within a semiclassical instanton framework incorporating Floquet modulation and Ohmic environmental coupling, the tunneling exponent factorizes into a system-dependent static contribution and a universal function of two dimensionless control parameters: normalized driving frequency and dissipation strength. This factorization arises from the combined modification of a single saddle-point trajectory and introduces no additional independent scaling variables. Weak-to-moderate dissipation acts as a smooth dynamical renormalization of the effective action, preserving the saddle-point structure and enabling controlled analytical expansion. In the high-frequency regime, the response exhibits universal dynamical averaging, while an explicit integral representation establishes a continuous adiabatic to Floquet crossover. Direct numerical evaluation of the nonlocal instanton action confirms that the normalized tunneling exponent exhibits a universal dependence on the driving parameters across different model systems. These results identify driven dissipative barrier crossing as a distinct two-parameter universality class within nonlinear nonequilibrium dynamics and provide a predictive functional framework for response phenomena in driven systems with memory.
tldr: The paper shows that barrier-crossing (tunneling) in periodically driven dissipative systems is governed by an explicit two-parameter universal response function within a semiclassical instanton/Floquet framework.
motivation: Universality in nonlinear nonequilibrium systems is well established through scaling laws, but whether it survives when periodic forcing and nonlocal dissipative memory act simultaneously is an open question in driven open dynamics.
method: A semiclassical instanton approach incorporating Floquet modulation and Ohmic environmental coupling is used, with the tunneling exponent factorizing into a static system-dependent part and a universal function of normalized driving frequency and dissipation strength; direct numerical evaluation of the nonlocal instanton action tests this.
result: The normalized tunneling exponent exhibits a universal dependence on the two dimensionless control parameters across different model systems, with weak-to-moderate dissipation acting as a smooth dynamical renormalization of the effective action and high-frequency driving producing universal dynamical averaging.
conclusion: Driven dissipative barrier crossing is identified as a distinct two-parameter universality class in nonlinear nonequilibrium dynamics, providing a predictive functional framework for response phenomena in driven systems with memory.

title: Gravitationally Induced Entanglement Of Matter In Quadratic Curvature Gravity And Constraints On Ghost Mass
authors: Linda M. van Manen, Tim Blankenstein, Anupam Mazumdar
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22501v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate gravitationally generated entanglement in two quantum harmonic oscillators induced by quadratic (Stelle) gravity, including corrections up to [MATH] post-Newtonian order. Starting from the quadratic action, we derive the effective two-body Hamiltonian for two harmonically trapped masses, incorporating the contributions of the massive spin-[MATH] ghost ([MATH]) and massive spin-[MATH] ([MATH]) degrees of freedom of the gravitational field. For two quantised oscillators prepared in their ground state, we compute the von Neumann and R\'enyi entropies of the reduced state and identify a frequency at which the gravitationally-induced entanglement vanishes due to cancellation between relativistic momentum squeezing and quantum-delocalisation-induced position squeezing. We further analyze the cancellation frequency and derive the approximate constraint [MATH] for the spin-[MATH] and spin-[MATH] modes. This relation follows from demanding a stable harmonic oscillator description. Finally, we study gravitationally-induced concurrence in a non-Gaussian setup and show how quadratic gravity modifies the entanglement generated between two spatial superpositions. The concurrence can approach [MATH] for certain choices of mass, spatial superposition, particle distance, and spin-[MATH] and spin-[MATH] modes. The concurrence will deviate from Newtonian gravity at certain particle separations, depending on the energy of the spin-[MATH] and spin-[MATH] modes. For example, spin modes as low as [MATH] eV become distinguishable from Newtonian gravity at a distance [MATH]m. This allows us to constrain the spin-[MATH] and spin-[MATH] masses in experiments.
tldr: The paper computes gravitationally induced entanglement between two harmonic oscillators in quadratic curvature (Stelle) gravity to constrain the masses of spin-2 ghost and spin-0 modes.
motivation: To understand how quadratic curvature corrections to gravity affect gravitationally induced entanglement and to derive experimental constraints on ghost and scalar modes.
method: Derive an effective two-body Hamiltonian up to post-Newtonian order from the quadratic action, compute von Neumann and Rényi entropies for ground-state oscillators, and analyze concurrence in a non-Gaussian setup with spatial superpositions.
result: A cancellation frequency is found where entanglement vanishes due to competing squeezing effects, leading to an approximate constraint on the ghost mass; concurrence deviates from Newtonian gravity at certain separations, allowing constraints on spin modes.
conclusion: Quadratic gravity modifications can be probed via entanglement measurements, offering a way to constrain ghost and scalar mode masses with future experiments.

title: Thermometry In Near-Degenerate Nitrogen-Vacancy Ensembles Enabled By Bright-Dark-State Mixing
authors: John O. Dabiri Matt K. Fu
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22661v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers have emerged as a highly sensitive platform for spatially resolved temperature measurements. When the [MATH] and [MATH] transitions are nearly degenerate and the Rabi frequency is comparable to the transition splitting, the spin dynamics encountered during pulsed protocols for temperature measurement can significantly alter the intended accumulation of temperature-dependent phase. We investigate these triplet ([MATH], [MATH]) spin dynamics and their effect on pulsed thermometry protocols under these conditions. We find that the conventional thermal-echo timing produces negligible temperature-sensitive signal amplitudes at the common-mode detuning. However, we find that the nominal spin-echo timing produces resolvable oscillations at the common-mode detuning, leading to a strong temperature-sensitive carrier signal. This departure from the expected protocol behavior is qualitatively captured by an ensemble model of the triplet dynamics, which supports significant dark-state leakage as a plausible mechanism for the temperature-sensitive response. This mixing-enabled thermal echo uses a four-phase quadrature readout that resolves the signed oscillation frequency and is validated using independent sweeps of the microwave carrier frequency and fluid temperature. We further assess the ability of a four-refocusing-pulse (LDD4B) low-field dynamical-decoupling sequence to extend the NV coherence and find that while the echo retains a sensitivity to common-mode detuning, the effective phase-accumulation interval corresponds to approximately half the total evolution time. These findings could support the use of pulsed NV thermometry in biological or mobile applications where applying magnetic bias fields is impractical and microwave power may be limited.
tldr: The paper studies triplet spin dynamics and bright-dark-state mixing in near-degenerate NV ensembles to enable pulsed thermometry without magnetic bias fields.
motivation: NV centers are sensitive nanoscale thermometers, but near-degenerate transitions and limited microwave power complicate conventional pulsed thermometry protocols.
method: The authors model and measure NV ensemble spin dynamics under pulsed thermal-echo and spin-echo sequences, including a four-phase quadrature readout and an LDD4B dynamical-decoupling sequence.
result: Conventional thermal-echo timing yields negligible signal at common-mode detuning, whereas nominal spin-echo timing produces resolvable temperature-sensitive oscillations attributed to dark-state leakage.
conclusion: This mixing-enabled thermal echo could support practical NV thermometry in biological or mobile settings where bias fields are impractical and microwave power is limited.

title: Exact Realization Of Deep ReLU Computation In A Microscopic Statistical-Mechanical System
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22965v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Understanding the physical origin of the piecewise-linear computation in deep rectified linear unit (ReLU) networks remains a fundamental challenge. Here we establish an exact statistical-mechanical realization of arbitrary ReLU networks. Starting from a microscopic configuration space and its state multiplicities, we construct a partition function without prescribing a neural-network activation function. The resulting system admits equivalent descriptions in terms of cascaded quantum operations with post selection, or fermionic transport model. We rigorously prove that in [MATH] limit, the thermodynamic observables of this system exactly reproduce the hidden states, outputs, and loss function of an arbitrary deep ReLU network. Crucially, we demonstrate that the piecewise-linear behavior of the ReLU network emerges from a first-order phase transition in the microscopic system, where the discontinuities precisely coincide with the boundaries of linear regions of ReLU network. This work establishes an exact physical foundation for deep neural computation and provides a novel statistical-mechanical perspective on neural architecture design.
tldr: The paper constructs an exact statistical-mechanical realization of arbitrary deep ReLU networks, linking ReLU piecewise linearity to a first-order phase transition.
motivation: To understand the physical origin of piecewise-linear computation in deep ReLU networks and provide a physical foundation for neural computation.
method: Starts from a microscopic configuration space and state multiplicities to build a partition function, with equivalent descriptions via cascaded quantum operations with postselection or a fermionic transport model.
result: In a thermodynamic limit, thermodynamic observables exactly reproduce hidden states, outputs, and loss of arbitrary deep ReLU networks; ReLU linear-region boundaries coincide with discontinuities of a first-order phase transition.
conclusion: The work offers a novel statistical-mechanical perspective on neural architecture design and an exact physical foundation for deep neural computation.

title: One-Shot Information Hiding And Compound Wiretap Channels
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22439v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, due to the growing reliance on large amounts of data that are communicated, analyzed, and utilized, which inherently contain sensitive and personal information, secrecy and privacy in communication have become increasingly important. We present nonasymptotic information-theoretic analyses of two fundamental secrecy problems under channel uncertainties: the information hiding problem and the compound wiretap channel. The former admits a game-theoretic formulation, where one party (an information hider and a decoder) seeks to embed secret messages into a host signal for later reconstruction, while the opposing party (an attacker) attempts to remove or degrade the embedded information. The latter generalizes Wyner's wiretap channel by allowing multiple potential channel states. The information hiding problem concerns active attacks during data transmission, while the compound wiretap channel addresses passive eavesdropping and information leakage. The two problems, both of which consider channels with uncertainties, can be studied under a unified framework by utilizing a covering argument and the Poisson matching lemma by Li and Anantharam. We derive novel one-shot achievability results for both problems that are applicable to any source distribution and any class of channels (not necessarily memoryless or ergodic), and that apply to both discrete and continuous cases. We also show that existing asymptotic results on both problems can be recovered by applying our results to discrete memoryless channels.
tldr: The paper provides one-shot information-theoretic achievability results for information hiding and compound wiretap channels under channel uncertainty using covering and Poisson matching arguments.
motivation: Growing reliance on sensitive data and unavoidable channel uncertainties motivate nonasymptotic secrecy analyses beyond standard memoryless or ergodic assumptions.
method: A unified framework based on a covering argument and the Poisson matching lemma is used to derive one-shot achievability bounds for any source distribution and any class of channels.
result: Novel one-shot achievability results are obtained for both active-attack information hiding and passive-eavesdropping compound wiretap channels, applicable to discrete and continuous settings, and existing asymptotic results for discrete memoryless channels are recovered.
conclusion: The work offers general nonasymptotic secrecy guarantees for classical communication under uncertainty, but lacks a quantum information component.

title: A Near-Optimal Joint Lower Bound For Sparse Quantum Linear System Solvers
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum linear system solvers form one of the central algorithmic primitives in quantum computing, with applications ranging from differential equations and optimization to machine learning. Their cost is commonly measured through query complexity, which counts the number of oracle calls needed to access the input matrix. In the sparse-access model, this complexity is governed by three parameters: the condition number [MATH], the sparsity [MATH] of the input matrix, and the target precision [MATH]. The dependence on [MATH] and [MATH] is already well understood through the lower bound [MATH], which matches the best known scaling in these parameters. Once the sparsity [MATH] is included, however, the expected lower bound has long been conjectured to be [MATH]. Recent work by Mori et al. [Quantum Sci. Tech. 11 035063 (2026)] made an important step towards this goal by establishing the lower bound [MATH] for constant error [MATH]. In this work, we complete the picture and prove the full joint lower bound [MATH] in the sparse-access model, thereby establishing the anticipated dependence on all three parameters simultaneously.
tldr: The paper proves a near-optimal joint lower bound on the query complexity of sparse quantum linear system solvers, capturing the simultaneous dependence on condition number, sparsity, and precision.
motivation: Quantum linear system solvers are a central algorithmic primitive, and although the dependence on condition number and precision is well understood, the conjectured joint lower bound including sparsity had remained unproven.
method: Building on recent work by Mori et al. that established a lower bound for constant error, the author develops an improved adversary-style argument in the sparse-access oracle model to extend the bound to general precision.
result: The full joint lower bound in the sparse-access model is established, matching the anticipated scaling in all three parameters (condition number, sparsity, and precision) simultaneously.
conclusion: This completes the picture for sparse quantum linear system solvers, confirming the conjectured complexity scaling and providing a tight characterization of the query complexity for all three parameters.

title: Capacity Of A Mixed Multiple-Access Channel With Causal Observation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the capacity region of a mixed binary multiple-access channel whose receiver can choose how each observation is formed. Two ports reveal the sum modulo two of the transmitted symbols with retention probabilities [MATH]; their roles are interchanged by an unknown state that remains fixed during the block. With one observation per channel use, no transmitter feedback, and zero switching cost, the region is [MATH] for every fixed error threshold below one, and a strong converse holds. For error thresholds below one half, the largest open-loop sum rate is [MATH], whereas a fixed port permits only [MATH]. A causal receiver attains the larger region by learning the state from erasure flags while using every channel use for data. A posterior port rule makes only finitely many incorrect selections almost surely, with a uniformly bounded expected number of mistakes. Exact random linear-code formulas and output-counting converses quantify the finite-block consequences. At blocklength 256 with [MATH], independent numerical validation supports 214 message bits at a one-percent ensemble failure target, compared with 148 bits for the best open-loop allocation in the same code ensemble. The resulting 44.59\% increase is achieved with the same transmission and observation budgets. The analysis exhibits an explicit capacity gain from controlling the observation axis and separates that gain from information lost after a record has already been formed.
tldr: The paper determines the capacity region of a mixed binary multiple-access channel where the receiver can causally adapt its observation port, achieving a larger sum rate than open-loop strategies.
motivation: To understand whether and how causal control over the observation axis can increase communication capacity in a multiple-access channel with an unknown fixed state and erasure feedback.
method: Analyzes a two-port binary MAC where each port reveals the sum modulo two of transmitted symbols with given retention probabilities, deriving capacity regions, a strong converse, and exact random linear-code formulas for finite blocklengths.
result: For error thresholds below one half, a causal receiver attains a strictly larger sum rate than any fixed port; at blocklength 256, numerical validation supports 214 message bits versus 148 bits for the best open-loop allocation (44.59% increase).
conclusion: Controlling the observation axis yields an explicit capacity gain that is separated from information lost after a record has already been formed, with finite-block consequences quantified by random linear codes.

title: Physics-Informed Classical And Quantum Neural Networks For One-Dimensional Schrodinger Eigenvalue Problems
authors: Tariq Mahmood, Waqas Arshad, Bilal Naseer, Alfredo Raya
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22189v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Schrodinger equation in one spatial dimension admits a small set of exactly solvable potentials that serve as natural proving grounds for any new eigenvalue solver. We formulate Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and Physics-Informed Quantum Neural Networks (PIQNNs) for the time-independent Schrodinger equation and apply them to three of these benchmarks: the harmonic oscillator, the infinite square well, and the finite square well. In each case a composite loss encodes the differential-equation residual, the normalization condition, the boundary behavior, and the orthogonality between eigenstates, so that the trial wave function is driven toward a genuine eigenfunction without supervised data. The eigenvalues and wave functions returned by both methods are compared against the exact spectra and against three classical references: the matrix Numerov method, the finite difference method, and the shooting method. For the smooth oscillator the two neural solvers reproduce the lowest four eigenvalues to parts per million, while for the square wells they recover the analytic levels with comparable fidelity even where the potential is discontinuous. The quantum circuit, built as a layered angle-embedding ansatz with strongly entangling blocks, converges more reliably than its classical counterpart on the higher excited states, where the loss landscape of the classical network becomes harder to navigate.
tldr: Physics-informed classical and quantum neural networks are used to solve one-dimensional Schrödinger eigenvalue problems for benchmark potentials, achieving high accuracy and showing that quantum circuits converge more reliably for higher excited states.
motivation: The time-independent Schrödinger equation has only a few exactly solvable potentials, so new numerical solvers require thorough testing. Physics-informed neural networks offer a data-free approach, and quantum neural networks may improve optimization in challenging regimes.
method: The authors formulate physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) and physics-informed quantum neural networks (PIQNNs) with a composite loss encoding the differential-equation residual, normalization, boundary behavior, and orthogonality. They benchmark on the harmonic oscillator, infinite square well, and finite square well, comparing eigenvalues and wave functions against exact spectra and classical numerical methods (matrix Numerov, finite difference, shooting).
result: For the smooth oscillator, both neural solvers reproduce the lowest four eigenvalues to parts per million, and for the square wells they recover analytic levels with comparable fidelity even with discontinuous potentials. The quantum circuit, built as a layered angle-embedding ansatz with strongly entangling blocks, converges more reliably than its classical counterpart on higher excited states.
conclusion: Physics-informed quantum neural networks are effective for one-dimensional eigenvalue problems and can outperform classical networks in navigating difficult loss landscapes for excited states, though the study is limited to simple benchmark potentials.

title: From IceCube To IT-Sphere: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Gnn For Banking It Root Cause Analysis
authors: Antonio Greco, Riccardo Paoletti, Roberto Cappuccio, Mario Onorato
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present Hybrid Quantum Root Cause Analysis (HQ-RCA), an industrially grounded workflow for root cause analysis in banking IT operations, built on a hybrid Quantum Graph Neural Network (QGNN): the classical backbone of DynEdge (the IceCube neutrino-reconstruction GNN, which we call standalone DynEdge), with its classification head replaced by a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC). On 13 months of anonymised IT data (13k alarm clusters) from a major European bank, the hybrid QGNN matches standalone DynEdge -- the strongest classical baseline -- on [MATH], while standalone DynEdge leads the ranking metrics. A readout-sensitivity and layout-robustness study, analysed via Dimensional Expressivity Analysis (DEA), shows that the effective parameter dimensionality (rank) of the quantum observable has no measurable correlation with [MATH]; we therefore keep the simplest readout [MATH] (the Pauli-[MATH] expectation on the first qubit), which in the deployed layout is rank-1, collapsing optimisation to a 1-D problem solvable by a gradient-free grid scan. Execution on IBM Heron r2 (no error mitigation) shows this gradient-free readout is executable on NISQ hardware after threshold recalibration.
tldr: The paper introduces HQ-RCA, a hybrid quantum-classical graph neural network for root cause analysis in banking IT operations, using a variational quantum circuit as the classification head.
motivation: To apply quantum machine learning to industrial IT root cause analysis and evaluate whether a hybrid QGNN can match or improve upon a strong classical baseline on real alarm data.
method: The authors replace the classification head of the DynEdge GNN with a variational quantum circuit and test it on 13 months of anonymized alarm clusters from a major European bank, analyzing readout sensitivity and layout robustness via Dimensional Expressivity Analysis.
result: The hybrid QGNN matches standalone DynEdge on one metric but standalone DynEdge leads ranking metrics; the effective rank of the quantum observable shows no measurable correlation with performance, and the simplest Pauli-Z readout is executable on IBM Heron r2 after threshold recalibration.
conclusion: A gradient-free rank-1 readout is NISQ-executable, but the work remains an applied quantum machine learning study with no clear quantum information-theoretic contribution or demonstrated quantum advantage.

title: The Deterministic Broadcast Channel Revisited: A Bipartite Graph Approach
authors: Yiyu Qiu, Wei Chen, H. Vincent Poor
abstract: ArXiv:2609.23322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The general broadcast channel (BC) has attracted considerable attention because it is a central problem in network or multi-user information theory. The deterministic BC (det-BC), in which both output symbols are functions of the input symbol, plays a vital role in understanding general BCs. In the 1970s, Marton and Pinsker investigated the det-BC independently using a random coding approach and hence quantified its capacity region as functions of the entropy of output symbols. In this paper, we present a purely deterministic and combinatorial treatment of the deterministic BC, which is in contrast to Marton and Pinsker's probabilistic treatment. In particular, we show that each det-BC can be uniquely and completely characterized by a bipartite graph. Based on the bipartite graph model, we present the explicit capacity region of the general det-BC and a deterministic capacity-achieving coding scheme. Specifically, each point on the capacity region boundary is expressed as an explicit function of the degree sequences of the two parts, with boundary coordinates parametrized by the tangent slope. As a result, a closed-form capacity region, which was previously unknown except for special cases such as the Blackwell channel, can be analytically determined, without optimizing the probability distribution of input symbols numerically. For a bipartite graph consisting of multiple isolated subgraphs, there can exist a commonly decodable message while preserving the maximum achievable sum rate, and its achievable rate is explicitly characterized. Finally, the bipartite-graph formulation allows us to construct optimal finite-blocklength coding for the det-BC through binary linear programming.
tldr: The paper gives a purely deterministic and combinatorial characterization of the deterministic broadcast channel using bipartite graphs, yielding explicit capacity regions and finite-blocklength coding.
motivation: The deterministic broadcast channel is a central problem in classical network information theory, and prior capacity results by Marton and Pinsker used probabilistic random coding methods that left explicit closed forms unknown except in special cases.
method: Each deterministic broadcast channel is modeled by a bipartite graph, and the capacity region boundary is expressed explicitly in terms of the degree sequences of the two graph parts, with boundary coordinates parametrized by the tangent slope.
result: The authors obtain a closed-form capacity region for general deterministic broadcast channels, characterize a commonly decodable message for disconnected bipartite graphs, and construct optimal finite-blocklength codes via binary linear programming.
conclusion: The bipartite graph approach provides a deterministic and combinatorial alternative to probabilistic treatments, enabling analytic capacity characterization without numerical optimization of input distributions.

title: Feasibility And Optimum Recovery In Warm-start Quantum Optimization For A Drug-response Model On A Trapped-ion Processor
authors: Tanzir Hossain, Rajib Rana, Prabal Datta Barua, Abu Ali Ibn Sina, Niall Higgins, Pascal Elahi, Robert Sang, Bjorn W. Schuller
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a seven-compound drug-response model, warm-start quantum approximate optimization (QAOA) on IonQ Forte-1 returned valid assignments more often than random bitstrings, but this alone did not show effective optimization. Ideal QAOA raised optimum probability above uniform feasible sampling in only four of twelve reference circuits. Hardware often fell below its own noiseless circuits, while greedy search solved all hardware models within 200 objective evaluations. Expanded simulations showed a gain over feasible sampling in 28 of 35 CAMA-1 panels and none of four 647-V panels. Annealing solved all these panels in every seed. A Grover mixer preserved feasibility and improved optimum probability over feasible sampling in all ten tested models. We analyzed 25 completed tasks containing 5,300 shots from 18 circuits and 14 instances. The encodings use 6-35 qubits and at most 4,900 feasible assignments, which we enumerated to establish exact optima. Noiseless references now cover both the original six circuits and six wider circuits. At 35 qubits, with 4,900 feasible assignments, ideal feasibility was 35.85%, compared with 7 of 200 valid hardware outputs. Its ideal optimum probability was below both sampling controls. The circuits sample assignments in a model built from measured single-agent and pairwise responses.
tldr: Warm-start QAOA on a trapped-ion processor is tested on a drug-response model, but hardware results often fail to outperform feasible sampling and classical greedy or annealing methods.
motivation: To assess whether warm-start quantum optimization can effectively solve a practical drug-response model on current trapped-ion hardware, comparing against classical baselines.
method: The authors run warm-start QAOA with a Grover mixer on IonQ Forte-1, enumerate feasible assignments to establish exact optima, and compare noiseless simulations, hardware results, and annealing across multiple circuits and panels.
result: Hardware often yields valid assignments but rarely improves optimum probability over uniform feasible sampling; at 35 qubits ideal feasibility was 35.85% versus 7 of 200 valid hardware outputs, while annealing solved all tested panels.
conclusion: Warm-start QAOA on a current trapped-ion processor shows limited practical advantage for this drug-response model, with classical greedy and annealing methods proving more reliable.

title: Loss Induced Dynamics Of Optical Pulses In Saturable Nonlinear Media
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider pulse propagation in a saturable nonlinear coupler whose other arm is dissipative and other is transparent. A flow of energy from transparent to dissipative arm takes place for weak value of dissipation and the coupler losses its energy. The energy loss of the coupler reduces for strong dissipation. This energy loss depends on the saturable nonlinearity. We find that the flow of relative energy at the output of a finite-sized coupler has a peak at a particular value of nonlinear strength. The peak value decreases with the increase of dissipation and it vanishes for stronger dissipation due to Zeno effect.
tldr: The paper studies pulse propagation in a saturable nonlinear coupler with one dissipative and one transparent arm, showing energy flow and loss that depend on nonlinearity and dissipation, with a Zeno-effect suppression at strong dissipation.
motivation: To understand how loss and saturable nonlinearity jointly affect energy transfer and pulse dynamics in asymmetric nonlinear optical couplers.
method: The authors model pulse propagation in a coupler with saturable nonlinearity, one dissipative arm and one transparent arm, and analyze the energy flow and relative output energy as functions of nonlinear strength and dissipation.
result: Energy flows from the transparent to the dissipative arm for weak dissipation, causing coupler energy loss; the loss decreases for strong dissipation. The relative output energy peaks at a particular nonlinear strength, and this peak diminishes with increasing dissipation and vanishes for stronger dissipation due to the Zeno effect.
conclusion: Dissipation and saturable nonlinearity together control energy transfer and loss in such couplers, with the Zeno effect suppressing energy flow at strong dissipation.

title: Nagy And Pollard-Hilding-Type Stability Of Hilbert-Schmidt Frames
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22528v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish several sufficient conditions ensuring that a perturbed family of operators in a given Hilbert-Schmidt frame for a separable Hilbert space remains a Hilbert-Schmidt frame. The perturbation criteria are formulated through Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type inequalities, yielding explicit estimates for the resulting frame bounds. Several examples are presented to illustrate the applicability of the results.
tldr: The paper derives sufficient conditions under which perturbed families of operators remain Hilbert-Schmidt frames in separable Hilbert spaces, using Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type inequalities.
motivation: Frame theory provides redundant representations useful in signal processing and operator theory, and understanding the stability of frames under perturbation is essential for practical robustness.
method: The authors formulate perturbation criteria based on Nagy-type and Pollard-Hilding-type inequalities to establish conditions guaranteeing that a perturbed operator family remains a Hilbert-Schmidt frame.
result: Explicit estimates for the resulting frame bounds are obtained, and several examples illustrate the applicability of the perturbation criteria.
conclusion: The work extends classical frame stability results to the Hilbert-Schmidt frame setting with quantitative bounds on frame preservation under perturbation.

title: Sumset Structure In Local Computation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22732v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study a new model of decision trees that lies at the frontier of provable circuit lower bounds. We study [MATH]-local decision trees, in which each internal node queries an [MATH]-local function of the input. We show that sufficiently strong lower bounds for [MATH]-local decision trees would imply several breakthrough circuit lower bounds, including super-linear size lower bounds for log-depth circuits and improved bounds for unrestricted-depth circuits. Previously, such consequences were known to follow from strong lower bounds for depth-[MATH] circuits, which has been the main prior approach in attempting to prove these results. Since local decision trees are strictly weaker than depth-[MATH] circuits, this provides a formally easier route to the same circuit lower-bound consequences. We prove essentially optimal lower bounds for a weaker variant that we call oblivious [MATH]-local decision trees, where all nodes at the same depth query the same function. Our lower bounds follow from a new technique that uncovers sumset structure in local maps, and our hard functions are sumset dispersers, sumset condensers, and directional affine dispersers. Along the way, we give an explicit construction of a sumset condenser with small entropy loss. As an additional contribution, we initiate the study of degree-[MATH] decision trees, in which each query is a quadratic polynomial of the input. We show that proving lower bounds in this model is a natural stepping stone toward constructing dispersers for degree-[MATH] variety sources, which imply improved circuit lower bounds for unrestricted depth circuits. We prove nearly maximal lower bounds for the oblivious variant of the model.
tldr: The paper introduces local decision trees and uses sumset structure to prove lower bounds that would imply stronger classical circuit lower bounds.
motivation: The authors aim to find a formally easier route to breakthrough circuit lower bounds by studying decision trees whose queries are local functions rather than full depth-2 circuits.
method: They define k-local decision trees and oblivious variants, then develop a new sumset-structure technique for local maps to prove essentially optimal lower bounds for the oblivious model.
result: They show that strong lower bounds for local decision trees imply super-linear size lower bounds for log-depth circuits and improved bounds for unrestricted-depth circuits; they also give explicit sumset condensers with small entropy loss.
conclusion: The work establishes local decision trees as a promising frontier for classical circuit lower bounds and initiates degree-2 decision trees as a stepping stone toward dispersers for variety sources.

title: New Construction Of Power Functions With Low c-Differential Uniformity Over Finite Fields
authors: Zhiye Yang, Yan Wang, Keqin Feng
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22763v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the [MATH]-differential uniformity of power functions over finite fields, an important class of cryptographic functions with favorable differential properties. Specifically, for finite fields [MATH] satisfying [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH], we prove that there exists [MATH], where [MATH] is an [MATH]-th primitive root of unity in [MATH], the constructed power functions [MATH] with [MATH] and [MATH] satisfy the upper bound [MATH], provided that certain cyclotomic conditions hold. We show that our conditions are mild; namely, such power functions can be constructed over infinitely many extension fields [MATH] of [MATH] for any given [MATH] and prime [MATH] with [MATH]. Furthermore, based on the Weil bound for multiplicative character sums, we prove that the obtained upper bound is tight for sufficiently large [MATH], demonstrating the optimality of our results. We also analyze the special case [MATH] and derive simplified explicit conditions. In particular, we explicitly characterize the admissible parameters for the case [MATH] and present concrete function examples for practical validation.
tldr: The paper constructs new power functions over finite fields with provably low c-differential uniformity, a purely classical cryptographic property.
motivation: Power functions with low differential (and c-differential) uniformity are important in classical cryptography, particularly for designing S-boxes in block ciphers resistant to differential attacks.
method: The authors use cyclotomic conditions in finite fields, primitive roots of unity, and the Weil bound for multiplicative character sums to establish upper bounds and tightness.
result: They prove that certain power functions x^d satisfy a given upper bound on c-differential uniformity whenever mild cyclotomic conditions hold, over infinitely many extension fields, and show the bound is tight for large fields.
conclusion: The work advances classical finite-field cryptography by giving explicit constructions and optimality results for low c-differential uniformity power functions, with concrete examples for specific parameters.

title: All-optical Spin-selective Control And Shaping Of Frequency Conversion Pathways
authors: Xiaoxi Xu, Mai Tal, Danielle Ben-Haim, Tal Ellenbogen
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between optical spin and crystal symmetry provides a powerful mechanism to control light-matter interaction, enabling advances in imaging, holography, sensing, signal processing, and more. Here we reveal that this interplay can also be exploited as a programmable mechanism for selecting and shaping nonlinear frequency-conversion pathways. Using a z-cut lithium niobate thin film, we experimentally demonstrate spin-selective switching between complementary three-wave mixing pathways, where co- and cross-circular-polarization excitations activate sum- and difference-frequency generation, respectively. We further generalize this concept to establish a quantitative spin-to-frequency mapping, that encodes the pump spin composition into the generated frequencies, and enables the reverse retrieval of the pump spin state. Finally, we leverage this concept also to demonstrate mapping of spin patterns to a combination of frequency-dependent real space images, and Fourier-space diffraction patterns. These results pave the way for all-optical programable frequency-conversion and spatiotemporal nonlinear signal manipulation in free-space and integrated photonic systems.
tldr: The paper experimentally demonstrates all-optical spin-selective control and shaping of nonlinear frequency-conversion pathways in a lithium niobate thin film.
motivation: To exploit the interplay between optical spin and crystal symmetry as a programmable mechanism for selecting and shaping nonlinear frequency-conversion pathways.
method: Using a z-cut lithium niobate thin film, they switch between sum- and difference-frequency generation via co- and cross-circular-polarization excitations, and establish a quantitative mapping from pump spin to generated frequencies.
result: They achieve spin-selective switching between complementary three-wave mixing pathways, quantitative spin-to-frequency mapping with reverse retrieval, and mapping of spin patterns to frequency-dependent real-space images and Fourier-space diffraction patterns.
conclusion: The results pave the way for all-optical programmable frequency conversion and spatiotemporal nonlinear signal manipulation in free-space and integrated photonic systems.

title: Sectorial Finitely Generated Dynamical Frames
authors: Ilya Krishtal, Javad Mashreghi, Brendan Miller

motivation: Dynamical sampling and orbit-generated frames are central objects in applied harmonic analysis, and prior work has largely treated single generating vectors or special operator classes; a unified treatment via essential-spectrum localization allows sharp density thresholds to be formulated.
method: The authors use principal-logarithm real powers, sectorial spectrum assumptions, semi-Fredholm/Fredholm index theory, and a compact-perturbation reduction to projected vector-valued exponentials on an arc; generalized divided differences and divided-difference preconditioning handle collisions and multiplicities.
result: They show that fractional-orbit synthesis reduces to exponential synthesis on an arc, yielding frame conditions via one-sided lower uniform density and logarithmic block density, sharp raw-sampling density ranges (e.g. 0 to 5/4 for some essential-spectrum configurations, and 0 to 1/2 unrestricted), and an equivalence between the complement property at the critical density and a finite channel-cyclic condition with phase-retrieval consequences.

title: Cascaded Brillouin-Kerr Microcombs In Surface Nanoscale Axial Photonic Resonators
authors: Emily Eadie, Juan Diego Mazo-V\'asquez, Sophia Padvaiskas, Flore K. Kunst, Lewis Hill, Pablo Bianucci
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22629v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface nanoscale axial photonic resonators (SNAPRs) provide an axially structured whispering-gallery-mode platform in which nanoscale effective-radius variations produce spatially localized optical resonances. Here, we demonstrate cascaded Brillouin-Kerr microcomb generation in a SNAPR fabricated from 660 micrometer diameter silica fiber. Under continuous-wave pumping, cascaded stimulated Brillouin scattering generates first- and second-order Stokes fields that seed Kerr four-wave mixing within the cavity. The resulting nonlinear spectrum contains two comb families with a common azimuthal spacing of 100.2 GHz and a relative offset of 9.6 GHz, consistent with the Brillouin shift in silica. A low-power transmission spectrogram provides a spatially resolved modal analysis of the resonator, revealing localized resonances with loaded quality factors on the order of ten million, and optical resonance pairs compatible with the measured Brillouin spacing. These results establish SNAPRs as a platform for studying cascaded stimulated Brillouin scattering, Kerr four-wave mixing, and comb formation in axially structured whispering gallery resonators.
tldr: The paper demonstrates cascaded Brillouin-Kerr microcomb generation in surface nanoscale axial photonic resonators (SNAPRs) using silica fiber.
motivation: SNAPRs offer an axially structured whispering-gallery-mode platform with localized resonances, motivating studies of nonlinear optical processes such as Brillouin scattering and Kerr comb formation.
method: Continuous-wave pumping of a 660 μm diameter silica fiber SNAPR excites cascaded stimulated Brillouin scattering, which seeds Kerr four-wave mixing and produces a dual-family microcomb spectrum.
result: Two comb families with a 100.2 GHz azimuthal spacing and a 9.6 GHz relative offset are observed, consistent with the Brillouin shift in silica, alongside resonances with quality factors around 10^7.
conclusion: The work establishes SNAPRs as a platform for investigating cascaded Brillouin-Kerr nonlinear dynamics and comb formation in axially structured whispering-gallery resonators.

title: Rubidium Referenced Kerr Comb With Cavity Phase Matching
authors: Xinwei Yi, Kunpeng Jia, Jingru Ji, Zhong Yan, Biaobing Jin, Zhenlin Wang, Wei Liang, Shi-Ning Zhu, Zhenda Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22692v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phase matching is a fundamental problem in nonlinear optics that is normally constrained by material dispersion. The limited operation wavelengths within phase matching window limits the application, including the precise metrology using Kerr combs. Demanding applications like compact optical clock and astronomical spectroscopy requires atomic reference around 800 nm, where the natural phase matching is challenging. Here we revisit the concept of cavity phase matching (CPM), and fully reveal its advantage to engineer artificial phase matching beyond material dispersion. With the access of CPM condition in a monolithic high-Q fiber Fabry-P\'erot resonator featuring a macroscopic cavity length, we achieve low noise Kerr comb generation around 800 nm, within the power budget of a single-mode laser diode. Inside a pump-integrated package of 19 cm3, low phase noise of -125 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz offset frequency is achieved for a 10.1 GHz repetition rate. Most importantly, the generated Kerr comb has been directly referenced to rubidium atomic transition for long-term stable operation. This result not only opens a new way for Kerr comb generation at arbitrary wavelengths, but also can be generalized to any other nonlinear optical frequency conversion application.
tldr: Demonstrates low-noise Kerr comb generation at 800 nm via cavity phase matching in a fiber Fabry-Pérot resonator, referenced to rubidium for long-term stability.
motivation: Material dispersion limits phase-matching windows for Kerr combs, making atomic-referenced operation around 800 nm challenging for applications like compact optical clocks and astronomical spectroscopy.
method: The authors revisit cavity phase matching (CPM) in a monolithic high-Q fiber Fabry-Pérot resonator with macroscopic cavity length, generate a Kerr comb using a single-mode laser diode, and package the pump-integrated system for rubidium referencing.
result: They achieve low phase noise of -125 dBc/Hz at 100 kHz offset for a 10.1 GHz repetition rate within a 19 cm3 package, with the comb directly referenced to a rubidium atomic transition for long-term stable operation.
conclusion: This approach enables Kerr comb generation at arbitrary wavelengths beyond material dispersion constraints and can be generalized to other nonlinear optical frequency conversion applications.

title: The Doublet Tower Of Cl(4,2): Universal Nilpotency, Projector Identities, And The sl(8,R) Parabolic From Conformal Null Vectors

We prove that the ad_D-eigenvectors of Cl(4,2), those elements with eigenvalue~[MATH] under the Lie bracket [MATH], are exhausted by 16 doublets of the form [MATH], where [MATH] is a null vector and [MATH] is a product of Lorentz-sector basis vectors indexed by [MATH]. These doublets satisfy universal algebraic identities: [MATH] (nilpotency) and [MATH] (single-projector proportionality), where [MATH], [MATH] is the spectator metric, and [MATH]. The contracted sums [MATH] are shown to be controlled by the elementary symmetric polynomials [MATH] of the Lorentz signature values [MATH], with the vanishing of [MATH] reflecting the [MATH] signature of physical spacetime. tldr: The paper studies the algebraic structure of doublets in the conformal geometric algebra Cl(4,2), proving nilpotency and projector identities and showing that these doublets generate sl(8,R).
motivation: The work aims to uncover universal algebraic identities and Lie-algebraic structures hidden in conformal geometric algebra, with connections to conformal null vectors and physical spacetime signature.
method: The authors analyze the ad_D-eigenvectors of Cl(4,2), derive doublet identities, and compute commutator spans across conformal extensions Cl(p+1,q+1) to identify the missing center.
result: They exhaust the doublet eigenvectors, prove universal nilpotency and projector proportionality, and show that the 32 doublets generate the 63-dimensional Lie algebra sl(8,R) containing so(4,2).
conclusion: The doublet tower provides a unified framework for conformal algebra and its extensions, with applications to Dirac/Majorana dichotomies; however, the work is primarily mathematical and not directly aligned with quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Interference-Free Capacity Of A Binary Interference Channel With Causal Observation
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We determine the capacity region of a two-user binary interference channel with receiver-controlled observation and prove that causal port selection attains the interference-free limit. The physical--observation dual-axis formulation makes the observation kernel a design variable subject to explicit causal and resource constraints. For two equiprobable, initially unknown block states, matching converses and coding constructions give exact sum capacities of 1, [MATH], and 2 bits per channel use for fixed-port, open-loop, and causal policies, respectively. These results hold for every fixed joint error threshold below [MATH], under both average and maximal message error, with error averaged over the block state. Every receiver makes one observation per slot and switches ports at most once; the transmitters receive no feedback and the receivers do not cooperate. Causal observation thus doubles the optimal fixed-port sum capacity and exceeds the optimal open-loop sum capacity by 50\%. With independent erasures of retention probability [MATH], the exact causal region is [MATH]. A finite-blocklength bound accounts jointly for state-identification pilots and coding redundancy. We also optimize observation policies for fixed codes: an exact finite-horizon solution reduces message error from 10.76\% to 7.52\%, and a second-order approximation bound controls optimization over continuous observation directions. Linear-array designs and coding experiments examine the corresponding training, reliability, and control costs. The capacity result identifies a setting in which observation design removes the entire interference penalty, with the gain established by a converse as well as an achievable construction.
tldr: Determines the capacity region of a two-user binary interference channel with causal receiver observation, showing that causal port selection attains the interference-free limit.
motivation: To understand how receiver-controlled observation and causal port selection can mitigate interference in a classical interference channel.
method: Formulates a dual-axis (physical and observation) model, derives exact sum capacities for fixed-port, open-loop, and causal policies, and optimizes observation policies.
result: Causal observation doubles the optimal fixed-port sum capacity and exceeds the optimal open-loop sum capacity by 50%, with exact capacity regions for independent erasures.
conclusion: Observation design can eliminate the entire interference penalty, with gains established by converse and achievable construction.

The same holds for a uniform subset of prescribed cardinality, and for discrete Fourier and real Hadamard matrices. At fixed accuracy the bound removes one sparsity logarithm from the earlier count and replaces [MATH] by [MATH]; for Walsh matrices it matches, up to constants, the lower bound of B\l asiok et al.\ in their range. motivation: The restricted isometry property is central to compressed sensing and signal recovery, and sharper bounds can improve sampling requirements for structured matrices.
method: The authors employ entropic mirror descent as a proof mechanism, analyzing Bernoulli row selection and uniform subsets via a relative-entropy potential to control amplitude predictor corrections.

conclusion: The work advances mathematical harmonic analysis and compressed sensing but has no apparent connection to quantum information, information thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Tick-Tock On The Open Fronthaul: Securing Synchronization In O-ran
authors: Yiwei Zhang, Enrico Pisanti, Imtiaz Karim, Subangkar Karmaker Shanto, Elisa Bertino
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22525v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Precision Time Protocol (PTP) provides the time and phase synchronization required by disaggregated Open Radio Access Networks (O-RAN). Yet, in current open fronthaul deployments, PTP traffic lacks mandatory authentication and integrity protection, leaving synchronization vulnerable to spoofing, replay, and delay manipulation attacks that can degrade radio access performance. Existing protections are poorly suited to this setting: they either add excessive latency, do not support multicast dissemination efficiently, or fail to contain key exposure under partially trusted RUs. This paper analyzes the security risks of unprotected O-RAN PTP and develops a threat model for open fronthaul deployments. We then introduce PRTESLA-C, a lightweight synchronization protection mechanism that combines per-round delayed key disclosure with ASCON-based message authentication. PRTESLA-C uses an apply-then-verify-and-correct paradigm: timing samples are applied immediately to preserve real-time control, verified after key disclosure, and removed from persistent synchronization state if authentication fails. This design maintains sub-microsecond synchronization accuracy, provides strong protection against spoofing and replay, and bounds the impact of delay manipulation with minimal computational and latency overhead.
tldr: The paper analyzes security vulnerabilities in O-RAN fronthaul PTP synchronization and proposes PRTESLA-C, a lightweight delayed-key authentication mechanism using ASCON.
motivation: Open fronthaul deployments in O-RAN lack mandatory authentication and integrity protection for PTP traffic, exposing synchronization to spoofing, replay, and delay manipulation attacks that can degrade radio performance.
method: The authors develop a threat model for O-RAN PTP and introduce PRTESLA-C, which combines per-round delayed key disclosure with ASCON-based message authentication and an apply-then-verify-and-correct paradigm to preserve real-time synchronization.
result: PRTESLA-C maintains sub-microsecond synchronization accuracy, provides strong protection against spoofing and replay, bounds delay manipulation impact, and incurs minimal computational and latency overhead.
conclusion: The proposed mechanism secures O-RAN fronthaul synchronization without sacrificing real-time performance, offering a practical security solution for disaggregated RAN deployments.

title: Black-Box Attack For IRS-Aided Communications With BER-Only Feedback
authors: Jimmy Huang Zhengkai Tu (the Chinese University Of Hong Kong)
abstract: ArXiv:2609.23112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) has emerged as a promising wireless technology for enhancing legitimate communications. In this paper, we investigate an IRS-assisted multiuser MISO downlink network in which an attacker reconfigures the IRS to degrade legitimate data transmission. Specifically, we consider a black-box attack setting in which the attacker has access to neither channel information nor symbol-level observations and can observe only the BER reported by each user. The objective of the attacker is to identify an IRS configuration that maximizes the minimum BER among all users under a limited budget of non-repeated tests. To address this BER-only black-box attack problem, we propose PRIS, an online search method that learns effective phase transitions from previous trials and progressively narrows the search from large-block modifications to single-element refinement. Specifically, an annealed user-balancing reward and prioritized replay are incorporated to exploit noisy BER feedback. Numerical results demonstrate that PRIS achieves a higher minimum BER than existing benchmarks.
tldr: The paper proposes PRIS, an online black-box search method that reconfigures an intelligent reflecting surface to maximize the minimum BER across users using only per-user BER feedback and no channel state information.
motivation: IRS is a promising technology for enhancing legitimate wireless communications, which makes it a target for adversarial reconfiguration; existing attack methods assume channel knowledge or symbol-level observations that are often unavailable in practice.
method: The attacker problem is cast as a budget-constrained black-box optimization over IRS phase configurations, solved by an online search that moves from large-block modifications to single-element refinement, using an annealed user-balancing reward and prioritized replay to handle noisy BER-only feedback.
result: Numerical simulations show that PRIS attains a higher minimum BER across users than existing benchmark attack strategies under a limited number of non-repeated tests.
conclusion: BER-only black-box optimization is an effective and practical route for degrading IRS-assisted multiuser MISO downlink transmissions, motivating robustness considerations in IRS deployments.

title: Many Proof Complexity Generators Inside One Demi-Bits Generator
authors: Xin Li, Hanlin Ren, Yan Zhong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.23228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a propositional proof system [MATH] and a polynomial-time function [MATH] ([MATH]), we say that [MATH] is a *proof complexity generator* against [MATH] if [MATH] cannot efficiently prove the (suitably encoded) statement "[MATH]" for every [MATH], and [MATH] is a *demi-bits generator* against [MATH] if [MATH] cannot efficiently prove the statement "[MATH]" for a noticeable fraction of [MATH]. As can be seen from the definitions, proof complexity generators are qualitatively stronger objects than demi-bits generators. Our main result is that, perhaps counter-intuitively, every demi-bits generator "contains" exponentially many proof complexity generators. In fact, a random subset of output bits of a demi-bits generator forms a proof complexity generator with constant probability. This result is an extremely simple corollary of Pajor's Lemma (a strengthening of the well-known Sauer--Shelah Lemma). This result allows us to exhibit the hardness of the Range Avoidance problem ([MATH]) in several new, restricted settings of interest. Along the way, we introduce the notion of *zero-error disperser families* that can transform demi-bits generators into proof complexity generators, and show that this family can be computed by projections (i.e., without any circuit complexity overhead). Using a different instantiation of this family, we construct proof complexity generators from *barely non-trivial* demi-bits generators [MATH], where the number of hard-to-prove statements of the form "[MATH]" just slightly exceeds [MATH] (which is the number of *false* statements of this form).
tldr: Every demi-bits generator against a propositional proof system contains exponentially many proof complexity generators, shown via a simple corollary of Pajor's Lemma.
motivation: Proof complexity generators are qualitatively stronger than demi-bits generators, so it is surprising that the weaker objects can contain the stronger ones; this connection also yields new hardness results for the Range Avoidance problem.
method: The authors apply Pajor's Lemma (a strengthening of the Sauer–Shelah Lemma) to random subsets of output bits of a demi-bits generator, and introduce zero-error disperser families computable by projections to convert demi-bits generators into proof complexity generators.
result: A random subset of output bits of a demi-bits generator forms a proof complexity generator with constant probability; this exhibits Range Avoidance hardness in several new restricted settings and constructs proof complexity generators from barely non-trivial demi-bits generators.
conclusion: The work reveals an unexpected structural relationship between proof complexity and demi-bits generators, with applications to the Range Avoidance problem and a new notion of zero-error disperser families.

title: GNN-Based Global Csi Reconstruction For Fronthaul-Limited Distributed Mimo Systems
authors: Haojin Li, Kaiqian Qu, Anbang Zhang, Chen Sun, Wenqi Zhang, Haijun Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.23365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Global channel state information (CSI) acquisition is essential for cooperative precoding in distributed multiple-input multiple-output (DMIMO) systems, but uploading full instantaneous CSI from all distributed antennas creates heavy fronthaul overhead. This paper proposes a fronthaul-efficient acquisition framework based on graph neural network (GNN) reconstruction and task-driven antenna selection. Each transmission and reception point (TRP) uploads only selected antenna CSI, while the centralized unit (CU) reconstructs the full global CSI from partial observations. A universal mask-conditioned GNN is trained with random upload masks, used to evaluate antenna subsets under a fronthaul budget, and then fine-tuned for the selected deployment mask. Simulation results show improved CSI reconstruction accuracy with lower fronthaul and pilot overhead.
tldr: A graph neural network framework reconstructs global channel state information in fronthaul-limited distributed MIMO systems using partial antenna CSI uploads and task-driven antenna selection.
motivation: Global CSI is needed for cooperative precoding in distributed MIMO, but uploading full instantaneous CSI from all distributed antennas causes prohibitive fronthaul overhead.
method: A universal mask-conditioned GNN is trained with random upload masks, used to evaluate antenna subsets under a fronthaul budget, and fine-tuned for the selected deployment mask; each TRP uploads only selected antenna CSI and the CU reconstructs the full global CSI.
result: Simulations show improved CSI reconstruction accuracy with lower fronthaul and pilot overhead compared to baselines.
conclusion: GNN-based reconstruction combined with task-driven antenna selection offers a fronthaul-efficient solution for global CSI acquisition in distributed MIMO.

title: Mass In The Light Of Special Relativity
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22382v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The text analyzes the concept of mass within Special Relativity, initially deconstructing the interpretation of Einstein's equation ([MATH]) as a principle of equivalence. Based on the adoption of the conservation laws of momentum and energy, the non-additivity of mass in composite systems is established. While in atomic and nuclear systems the total mass is less than the sum of its constituents, in the subnuclear domain the opposite occurs: the positive potential energy of confinement of quarks causes the mass of a hadron to be greater than the sum of the masses of its quarks; in the case of nucleons, it is much greater. It is concluded, then, that the mass of baryonic matter in the observable Universe comes, for the most part, from the energy associated with strong interactions.
tldr: A conceptual analysis of mass in special relativity arguing that mass is non-additive in composite systems and that baryonic mass arises largely from strong-interaction confinement energy.
motivation: To clarify the meaning of mass in special relativity and to challenge the simple interpretation of E=mc^2 as a general equivalence principle.
method: The authors deconstruct the equivalence interpretation of Einstein's mass-energy relation and use conservation laws of momentum and energy to establish non-additivity of mass in composite systems.
result: They show that total mass differs from the sum of constituent masses: negative binding energy in atomic/nuclear systems reduces mass, while positive confinement energy in hadrons increases it, with nucleon masses dominated by quark confinement effects.
conclusion: The paper concludes that most of the mass of baryonic matter in the observable Universe originates from energy associated with strong interactions rather than from the intrinsic masses of quarks.

title: Stochastic Consensus Dynamics For Decentralized Decision Systems
authors: Andr\'e L. M. Vilela, Caio B. L. Silva, Kenric P. Nelson, Emilio Cobanera, Gaogao Dong
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22454v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A fundamental mechanism underlying collective phenomena in social, technological, and economic systems is decentralized decision-making, in which the behavior of individual agents follows from local interactions in the absence of central coordination. Consensus formation is a central feature of such systems, with relevance to blockchain networks, distributed artificial intelligence, autonomous multi-agent systems, distributed control, and collective decision networks. We investigate consensus formation using a stochastic consensus model on random networks and examine how initial conditions, network connectivity, and system size shape the emergence of unanimous states. We show that the stochastic dynamics strongly amplify small initial majorities, progressively suppress the competing state, and drive the system toward a predictable collective outcome. Network connectivity primarily controls the efficiency of this process: increasing connectivity accelerates the propagation of local agreement and reduces the likelihood that fluctuations reverse the initially dominant state, although these gains gradually saturate in highly connected networks. System size produces a complementary effect. Larger networks require more individual updates to reach unanimity, but they are also increasingly reliable in selecting the state favored by the initial majority. Finite-size analysis shows that the range of initial conditions associated with uncertain outcomes becomes progressively narrower as the network grows, decreasing approximately with the inverse square root of the system size. These results reveal a collective amplification mechanism by which weak initial asymmetries become increasingly decisive in large decentralized networks, and they provide a simple framework for understanding the efficiency, predictability, and reliability of consensus formation in distributed decision systems.
tldr: The paper studies a stochastic consensus model on random networks to understand how initial conditions, connectivity, and system size shape the emergence of unanimous states in decentralized decision systems.
motivation: Decentralized decision-making and consensus formation are central to social, technological, and economic systems, with applications in blockchain, distributed AI, and multi-agent systems.
method: The authors analyze a stochastic consensus dynamics on random networks, using finite-size scaling and simulations to examine the effects of initial majority, network connectivity, and system size.
result: Small initial majorities are amplified, competing states are suppressed, and larger or more connected networks accelerate and stabilize consensus, with the uncertain range shrinking as the inverse square root of system size.
conclusion: The findings reveal a collective amplification mechanism where weak initial asymmetries become decisive in large decentralized networks, offering a simple framework for understanding consensus efficiency and reliability.

title: Diffusion With Stochastic Resetting In The Presence Of A Delta Killing Trap: Drift-controlled Survival Regimes
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22527v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a one-dimensional diffusive particle subject to stochastic resetting to its initial position, in the presence of an imperfect, localized target that can absorb (kill) the particle, modeled by a delta-function killing rate. The central question is how stochastic resetting competes with drift-induced transience and the target's finite reactivity. Exact Laplace-space expressions are derived for the non-normalized propagator and survival probability, for arbitrary diffusion coefficient [MATH], resetting rate [MATH], and killing strength [MATH], first in the absence of drift and then under a constant drift. The long-time behavior separates into distinct regimes. Without resetting, unbiased diffusion exhibits the recurrent algebraic survival law [MATH], whereas any nonzero drift renders the motion transient with respect to the target and leaves a nonzero ultimate survival probability. By contrast, any [MATH] and [MATH] repeatedly renews encounters with the target and restores eventual absorption, yielding an exponential survival law [MATH]. The decay rate [MATH] is given by the dominant (rightmost) pole of the Laplace transform, and the surviving density converges after normalization to an explicit quasi-stationary profile. The driftless and perfectly absorbing limits recover standard resetting results. These formulas provide a unified description of the crossover between recurrence-controlled, transience-controlled, and renewal-controlled survival.
tldr: The paper studies one-dimensional diffusion with stochastic resetting in the presence of a delta-function killing trap, deriving exact survival probabilities and identifying distinct drift-controlled survival regimes.
motivation: The authors aim to understand how stochastic resetting competes with drift-induced transience and a target's finite reactivity, extending resetting theory to imperfect absorbing traps.
method: They derive exact Laplace-space expressions for the non-normalized propagator and survival probability for arbitrary diffusion coefficient, resetting rate, and killing strength, first without drift and then with constant drift, analyzing the dominant poles and quasi-stationary density.
result: Without resetting, unbiased diffusion gives an algebraic survival law, while any nonzero drift makes motion transient and yields nonzero ultimate survival; with resetting, encounters are renewed and survival becomes exponential with a decay rate set by the rightmost pole.
conclusion: The formulas provide a unified description of the crossover between recurrence-, transience-, and renewal-controlled survival, recovering standard resetting results in the driftless and perfectly absorbing limits.

title: Non-Polynomial Wave Computation Through Recurrent Resonant Scattering
authors: Junyu Zhu, Enzong Wu, Xiaomeng Li, Hongsheng Chen, Zuojia Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Structural nonlinearity enables nonlinear input--output mappings to emerge from otherwise linear wave dynamics. Repeated interactions with an input-encoded structure can enhance such mappings, but finite-depth implementations restrict the accessible functional order. Here we show that recurrent scattering in a resonant cavity provides a distinct regime for structural nonlinearity. Repeated interactions are coherently accumulated into a non-polynomial response to structural perturbations. The resulting mapping naturally takes a Kolmogorov--Arnold form: perturbation-induced resonance shifts realize the inner univariate mappings, while the resonant spectral response provides the outer mapping. We identify two complementary physical controls of representation capacity: the resonance linewidth governs the functional richness within each branch, whereas combining multiple branches expands the accessible function space. Microwave-cavity measurements validate the two-stage mapping and demonstrate a two-branch nonlinear computation through XOR classification. Our results connect recurrent resonant scattering with controllable non-polynomial computation in linear wave systems.
tldr: Recurrent resonant scattering in a microwave cavity is shown to enable non-polynomial wave computation via a Kolmogorov-Arnold-like two-stage mapping.
motivation: Structural nonlinearity in linear wave systems can produce nonlinear input-output mappings, but finite-depth implementations limit functional order; recurrent scattering may overcome this.
method: The authors use repeated coherent interactions in a resonant cavity to accumulate perturbation-induced resonance shifts as inner mappings and the resonant spectral response as an outer mapping, validated by microwave-cavity measurements.
result: Two-branch nonlinear computation is demonstrated with XOR classification, and resonance linewidth is identified as controlling functional richness within each branch.
conclusion: Recurrent resonant scattering connects to controllable non-polynomial computation in linear wave systems, offering a physical platform for wave-based computing.

title: Holomorphic Conformal Cartan Geometry: Conformal Gravity, Twistors, And Ambitwistors
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22861v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Four-dimensional conformal gravity, twistor theory, and ambitwistor theory are reviewed within the unified framework of holomorphic conformal Cartan geometry. Starting from the spinorial representation of the geometry, the normal [MATH]-valued Cartan connection, its curvature [MATH]-form, and the associated tractor bundles are systematically formulated. Evaluated on the real Lorentzian slice, the quadratic curvature action is shown to reproduce four-dimensional Weyl--Bach conformal gravity upon fixing a Weyl gauge. Local twistor and dual twistor bundles are constructed as associated spin tractor bundles, illustrating how parallel transport yields the classical incidence relations in flat space and chiral integrability constraints in curved backgrounds: anti-self-duality for [MATH]-surfaces and self-duality for [MATH]-surfaces. Furthermore, by pairing local twistors and dual twistors via an invariant canonical pairing, ambitwistor space is shown to parameterize complex null geodesics and symmetrically accommodate both left- and right-handed Weyl curvatures. This framework establishes a direct gauge-theoretic bridge linking conformal Cartan geometry to twistor and ambitwistor theories.
tldr: The paper reviews 4D conformal gravity, twistor theory, and ambitwistor theory within a unified holomorphic conformal Cartan geometry framework.
motivation: To provide a gauge-theoretic bridge linking conformal Cartan geometry to twistor and ambitwistor theories, aiming for a systematic formulation of conformal gravity and its twistor correspondences.
method: It uses spinorial representations of conformal Cartan geometry, constructs normal Cartan connections, curvature forms, tractor bundles, and local/dual twistor bundles, then explores parallel transport and canonical pairings.
result: The quadratic curvature action reproduces Weyl–Bach conformal gravity on the Lorentzian slice, and ambitwistor space parameterizes complex null geodesics while accommodating both chiralities of Weyl curvature.
conclusion: The framework establishes a direct gauge-theoretic link between conformal Cartan geometry and twistor/ambitwistor theories, potentially useful for mathematical physics but outside the researcher's quantum information and thermodynamics interests.

title: On Different Notions Related To Apn Mappings
authors: Ren\'e Rodr\'iguez-Aldama, Ajla \v{s}ehovi\'c, Enes Pasalic, Sadmir Kudin
abstract: ArXiv:2609.22394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An APN mapping [MATH] is a polynomial characterized by the non-vanishing property on 2-flats.
